item.title: 🚨 Blow for Bayern, star ruled out indefinitely!
item.description: 🚨 Blow for Bayern, star ruled out indefinitely! A major blow for Bayern Munich! Despite only coming on in the 68th minute against Arsenal yesterday, Luis Diaz had to leave the field in the 90th minute after suffering a thigh injury. This Thursday, Bayern Munich confirmed the bad news in a statement. The Colombian forward suffered a "minor hamstring tear". However, questions remain over Luis Diaz's return date, as Bayern Munich said their forward would be sidelined "indefinitely". The Bavarian club will therefore have to rely on youngster Lennart Karl, Serge Gnabry or Alphonso Davies. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Luis Díaz suffers muscle tear and is sidelined for now
item.description: Luis Díaz suffers muscle tear and is sidelined for now Bad news for FC Bayern Munich. Colombian forward Luis Díaz suffered a minor tear in his left hamstring during the Champions League match against Arsenal. The injury was confirmed by the club's medical department after the player underwent the necessary tests. The 29-year-old will be sidelined until further notice. The coach and Bayern fans will temporarily be without a key player in the team's attacking setup, right at a demanding stage of the season. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Champions League review: PSG take a hit, Man City’s empty seats and teenage hope for Liverpool
item.description: Phil Foden, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Rio Ngumoha made headlines this week. Composite: Getty, Reuters, Shutterstock A big week for … Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday , but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level. “Why me?” Kvaratskhelia asked his Instagram followers. The PSG policy of resting players in Ligue 1 to save them for the Champions League failed to protect him. By resting Rodri, Barcelona followed a wider practice among major clubs in European competition of saving stars’ legs for big domestic occasions. Barcelona face Real Madrid this weekend though Lamine Yamal is not being spared; his brilliant goal in Paris made it 10 goals, matched by 10 assists, from 10 matches. Related: Paris Saint-Germain sparkle on the pitch while the city of light burns around them | Barney Ronay Another heavyweight battle saw Arsenal lose Bukayo Saka to a first-half quad injury in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich . Declan Rice powered in a late equalizer after Harry Kane had put on a show that included a goal and an assist. Does the Ballon d’Or beckon for Kane? The prediction markets suggest so. Matching Barcelona’s perfect record this season at home and abroad are Manchester City, who continue to thrive amid infamy. A resurgent Phil Foden scored a hat-trick and new signing Allan impressed. The official crowd for their 5-1 defeat of AEK Athens was 40,402, but it looked smaller, and mockery duly descended on the club. There is mitigation for those who stayed away, including high ticket prices for Champions League matches in tough economic times, and a run of five home matches in 17 days. Still, City remain in the crosshairs, and the empty seats raise eyebrows for a club reporting record revenues. Equally, it is fair to point out that Anfield was not full, either, for Liverpool’s 4-3 defeat of Villarreal. A clean sweep of wins for Serie A, with three of their clubs scoring four goals. Inter let the side down with their 1-0 defeat of Shakhtar Donetsk. Roma defeated Slovan Bratislava 4-0, and Como beat Manchester United 4-1 , but the game of the week came in Naples. item.content:encoded: Phil Foden, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Rio Ngumoha made headlines this week. Composite: Getty, Reuters, Shutterstock A big week for … Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday , but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level. “Why me?” Kvaratskhelia asked his Instagram followers. The PSG policy of resting players in Ligue 1 to save them for the Champions League failed to protect him. By resting Rodri, Barcelona followed a wider practice among major clubs in European competition of saving stars’ legs for big domestic occasions. Barcelona face Real Madrid this weekend though Lamine Yamal is not being spared; his brilliant goal in Paris made it 10 goals, matched by 10 assists, from 10 matches. Related: Paris Saint-Germain sparkle on the pitch while the city of light burns around them | Barney Ronay Another heavyweight battle saw Arsenal lose Bukayo Saka to a first-half quad injury in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich . Declan Rice powered in a late equalizer after Harry Kane had put on a show that included a goal and an assist. Does the Ballon d’Or beckon for Kane? The prediction markets suggest so. Matching Barcelona’s perfect record this season at home and abroad are Manchester City, who continue to thrive amid infamy. A resurgent Phil Foden scored a hat-trick and new signing Allan impressed. The official crowd for their 5-1 defeat of AEK Athens was 40,402, but it looked smaller, and mockery duly descended on the club. There is mitigation for those who stayed away, including high ticket prices for Champions League matches in tough economic times, and a run of five home matches in 17 days. Still, City remain in the crosshairs, and the empty seats raise eyebrows for a club reporting record revenues. Equally, it is fair to point out that Anfield was not full, either, for Liverpool’s 4-3 defeat of Villarreal. A clean sweep of wins for Serie A, with three of their clubs scoring four goals. Inter let the side down with their 1-0 defeat of Shakhtar Donetsk. Roma defeated Slovan Bratislava 4-0, and Como beat Manchester United 4-1 , but the game of the week came in Naples. Scott McTominay scored twice, his first goals since a procedure on a benign heart arrhythmia as Napoli beat Bodø/Glimt 4-3 for their first win of the group stage. “I still need to find my best form, but I am not far away,” said McTominay. Player of the week Liverpool were a mess in the first 30 minutes against Villarreal and it was Rio Ngumoha who led the recovery. The 18-year-old played off the right, supplying two assists with his left foot: the long-term replacement for Mohamed Salah may already be at Anfield. Liverpool have nursed Ngumoha along, though this was his fifth start of the season. “Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo [Salah] last year was obviously massive,” Virgil van Dijk said of the teenager. Club in focus: Como With traditional Serie A giants Juventus and Milan in the Europa League, Como are enjoying their first season in the Champions League. If Manchester United were dreadful on Wednesday, Como’s rise hit its highest point yet. The club’s success carries echoes of Brighton and Bournemouth’s ascents, although Como’s is even more remarkable. They were a Serie D club in 2008, and the city is now known for something beyond its glorious scenery. Champions League winner Thierry Henry is among the investors in the club as is Como’s coach, Cesc Fàbregas, although the prime financiers are the Indonesian billionaire Hartono brothers. Jamestown Analytics, the Brighton owner Tony Bloom’s company, has been consulting Como. Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho and Antonio Conte are the elite coaches Fàbregas played under, and he has forged a high-pressing style against Italian orthodoxy. As United labored, they were swarmed by Como’s worker bees. Real Madrid have a buy-back option for Nico Paz, bought by Como in 2024, and the scorer of two fine goals against United. Argentina’s latest Messi replacement is rather beefier than his country’s idol. As Como deepened Michael Carrick’s plight, thoughts moved to potential replacements. Fàbregas has been mentioned, though United fans will recall the summer of 2013’s unsuccessful chase for him. Had a deal been done, his midfield partner would have been … Carrick. They said it Another week, another Manchester United PR crisis. This one involved Carrick hitting back at his players, a rarity in his managerial career. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” Bruno Fernandes said. Carrick’s riposte: “If you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.” On CBS, Jamie Carragher weighed, saying of Fernandes: “They all think he’s working hard. He’s not. He’s killing the rest of the team doing it.” The Amazon All or Nothing documentary series currently in production for United’s season will be appointment viewing. Looking ahead After two consecutive weeks of action, we have a fortnight off. Will Carrick still be at United by the time they host Roma on 3 November? Aston Villa, who have three wins from three and are second place in the table, have a glamour trip to Barcelona. Real Madrid, another side on three wins, travel to AEK. After defeat to Inter, Shakhtar’s adopted home, Stamford Bridge , hosts Sporting Lisbon, who this week were on the wrong end of Lask’s first ever group-stage win.

item.title: Sheehan switches to number eight for Munster derby
item.description: Sheehan will captain Ireland in next month's Nations Championship games in Caelan Doris' absence [Getty Images] Leinster captain Dan Sheehan will start at number eight for the first time in Saturday's United Rugby Championship interprovincial derby against Munster at the Aviva Stadium (18:00 BST). The Ireland hooker switches to the back row as one of four changes made by head coach Leo Cullen following last weekend's 48-23 Champions Cup victory over Clermont Auvergne. Ireland scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park makes his first appearance of the season, while former Munster out-half Joey Carbery earns his first start since rejoining Leinster. Ronan Kelleher and Jamie Osborne are also drafted into the starting side, with Kelleher replacing Sheehan at hooker and Osborne joining Robbie Henshaw in midfield. The hosts are seeking consecutive URC victories after bouncing back from opening defeats by the Lions and Sharks with a convincing win over Cardiff. Leinster have collected eight points from their opening three league matches, including four bonus points. Munster, meanwhile, have made seven changes to the side that defeated Racing 92 in the Champions Cup last weekend. Shane Daly returns from injury, while Josh Wycherley, Kieran Brookes, Fineen Wycherley, Jack O'Donoghue, Alex Kendellen and Gavin Coombes are also drafted into the starting XV. Former Ireland Under-20 international Sean O'Brien switches from the wing to outside centre as he prepares to make his 50th Munster appearance. Mark Donnelly is in line for his first appearance of the season from the replacements' bench, with academy centre Gordon Wood also among the replacements. Munster have recovered from their opening URC defeat by Glasgow Warriors with a victory over the Bulls and a 26-26 draw against Ulster on October 10. Munster: B O'Connor; McCarthy, S O'Brien, Nankivell, Daly; O'Shea, Casey; J Wycherley, Van der Merwe, Brookes; F Wycherley, Beirne (capt); O'Donoghue, Kendellen, Coombes. Replacements: Clein, Donnelly, Ala'alatoa, Edogbo, Gleeson, B O'Donovan, Hanrahan, Wood. Leinster: Keenan; T O'Brien, Osborne, Henshaw, J O'Brien; Carbery, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong; J McCarthy, Ryan; Baird, Van der Flier, Sheehan (capt). Replacements: G McCarthy, Usanov, Clarkson, O'Tighearnaigh, Penny, Gunne, Gabriel, Tector.

item.title: Henry: Not many people knew Como players, ‘it’s all down to Fabregas’
item.description: Henry: Not many people knew Como players, ‘it’s all down to Fabregas’ Arsenal legend Thierry Henry, one of Como’s minority shareholders, praises Cesc Fabregas not just as a coach, but also for signing ‘players that not a lot of people knew.’ Como beat Manchester United 4-1 in the Champions League Round 3 on Wednesday. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with teammates during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Nico Paz made headlines with two goals and one assist, but Como’s collective performance was impressive and dominant from the very beginning. The Argentine netted the opening goal after just two minutes, assisted Anastasios Douvikas in the second half, then scored his second of the night. Henry, an Arsenal and France national team legend, particularly enjoyed Como’s victory, being one of the club’s minority shareholders. “To see players like Jacobo Ramon, Yan Couto. People will talk about Nico Paz, or about Da Cunha because he plays for the French national team. But to be able to go and get players that not a lot of people knew, to make a team out of it. Look at where they are, where we are,” he said during the CBS Champions League Show. Thierry Henry and actor Terry Crews at the Stadio Sinigaglia watching the Serie A match between Como and Torino. “You can watch that every game in Italy. Cesc wants to dominate, put pressure. There’s a clear idea on and off the ball. This doesn’t mean you’ll win every single game, but when you watch the team, you know what they are about. They don’t panic.” Como finished fourth in Serie A last season, reaching Champions League qualification for the first time in their history. With six points from three Champions League matches so far this season, they are the better-placed Italian team in the league phase. “That’s what happened, and you arrive now beating Man United 4-1. Which doesn’t mean anything apart from the fact that you beat Man United 4-1, and that is also the biggest result in the history of the club. One of the best nights ever. You want more nights like that,” Henry continued. COMO, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 10: Cesc Fabregas, Manager of Como 1907, celebrates after the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Como 1907 and RB Leipzig at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) The Frenchman continued to highlight Fabregas’ influence in shaping the Como project. Henry is also a former Arsenal teammate of Fabregas. The duo played 100 games together for the Gunners. “How Cesc managed to put that team together. Now you’ll tell me Da Cunha is good,” Henry concluded. “You’ll tell me Nico Paz is good. Or Jacobo Ramon. But nobody told me that two years ago or three years ago, when they were in Serie B. That’s all down to Cesc

item.title: On this day: Fernando Alonso wins the world title, Michael Schumacher retires from F1
item.description: Motorsport photo On 22 October 2006, Fernando Alonso beat Michael Schumacher to the world title in the Brazilian Grand Prix, as the seven-time champion retired from Formula 1. In truth, there was little doubt Alonso was going to clinch a second crown that day. Schumacher’s engine failure and retirement from the lead of the Suzuka race had turned a potential two-point lead into a 10-point deficit, meaning the Ferrari racer needed both to win and his rival not to score at Interlagos. That endeavour took a turn for the worse when Schumacher encountered a fuel pressure problem in Q3, leaving him 10th on the grid with Alonso fourth. “I don't know what we can do,” the German said after qualifying. “I don't know how the race will develop. It is hard to predict something, but I will try my best. It is much more difficult starting from 10th, but of course I will try.” “Let's not forget that in the past, Michael has managed to win races starting even further back on the grid,” Ferrari technical director Ross Brawn added. That statement was inaccurate – across the preceding 248 races, Schumacher had won from outside the top 10 just once – but the Ferrari driver showed exactly why Brawn made it. He jumped from 10th to seventh on the first lap, then passed former team-mate Rubens Barrichello and overtook Giancarlo Fisichella around the outside for fifth on lap eight – meaning he was already right behind his title rival – but the slightest of touches with the Renault caused a rear-left puncture. Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Schumacher found himself down in 20th, 69 seconds adrift of race-leading team-mate Felipe Massa , while his deficit to Alonso was exactly one minute. By lap 27, he had caught the back of the pack and successively overtook Tiago Monteiro, Robert Doornbos, Nick Heidfeld and Robert Kubica , while undercutting other opponents and benefitting from retirements, to find himself fifth before his second pitstop. Emerging back out in seventh, Schumacher passed Barrichello again and pressured Fisichella into a lock-up in Turn 1 to claim fifth on lap 63. Massa’s commanding home drive meant he was still 33 seconds up the road, but second-placed Alonso was just eight seconds away from the recovering Ferrari. Schumacher ran out of laps to claim a podium finish but still performed a clinical move on McLaren ’s Kimi Raikkonen on the antepenultimate lap to take fourth position, as Alonso secured the championship. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo On 22 October 2006, Fernando Alonso beat Michael Schumacher to the world title in the Brazilian Grand Prix, as the seven-time champion retired from Formula 1. In truth, there was little doubt Alonso was going to clinch a second crown that day. Schumacher’s engine failure and retirement from the lead of the Suzuka race had turned a potential two-point lead into a 10-point deficit, meaning the Ferrari racer needed both to win and his rival not to score at Interlagos. That endeavour took a turn for the worse when Schumacher encountered a fuel pressure problem in Q3, leaving him 10th on the grid with Alonso fourth. “I don't know what we can do,” the German said after qualifying. “I don't know how the race will develop. It is hard to predict something, but I will try my best. It is much more difficult starting from 10th, but of course I will try.” “Let's not forget that in the past, Michael has managed to win races starting even further back on the grid,” Ferrari technical director Ross Brawn added. That statement was inaccurate – across the preceding 248 races, Schumacher had won from outside the top 10 just once – but the Ferrari driver showed exactly why Brawn made it. He jumped from 10th to seventh on the first lap, then passed former team-mate Rubens Barrichello and overtook Giancarlo Fisichella around the outside for fifth on lap eight – meaning he was already right behind his title rival – but the slightest of touches with the Renault caused a rear-left puncture. Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Schumacher found himself down in 20th, 69 seconds adrift of race-leading team-mate Felipe Massa , while his deficit to Alonso was exactly one minute. By lap 27, he had caught the back of the pack and successively overtook Tiago Monteiro, Robert Doornbos, Nick Heidfeld and Robert Kubica , while undercutting other opponents and benefitting from retirements, to find himself fifth before his second pitstop. Emerging back out in seventh, Schumacher passed Barrichello again and pressured Fisichella into a lock-up in Turn 1 to claim fifth on lap 63. Massa’s commanding home drive meant he was still 33 seconds up the road, but second-placed Alonso was just eight seconds away from the recovering Ferrari. Schumacher ran out of laps to claim a podium finish but still performed a clinical move on McLaren ’s Kimi Raikkonen on the antepenultimate lap to take fourth position, as Alonso secured the championship. Fernando Alonso, Renault, Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Fernando Alonso, Renault, Michael Schumacher, Ferrari “The race was chaotic, I think that is the right word,” Schumacher said. “We really had a superb car today, from the pure speed we could have lapped everybody. So I have to say it was the perfect end to the season in terms of car performance, but for me it didn't work out well.” Alonso hailed a “fantastic way” to conclude his time at Renault, which he described as “my family in Formula 1”, ahead of his long-awaited move to McLaren for 2007. “I will have these memories with them all my life, and to finish the last race like this is something that you never dream of, you never even try to dream of, because it's always more than what you expected,” he commented. Fernando Alonso, Renault Fernando Alonso, Renault With that career path, the Spaniard dreamt of emulating Ayrton Senna . “To join McLaren and never to race with Ferrari reminds me a lot of Senna,” he told TV channel Telecinco. “He won three titles, and for me, to retire with three and achieve what he achieved would be the objective of my career.” Twenty years on, Alonso is still chasing that third crown in F1. Meanwhile, Schumacher looked back on his glittering career, one month after announcing his retirement in Monza . With Ferrari signing Raikkonen for 2007, Schumacher staying would have come at the expense of youngster Massa, so he decided against it. But was there any chance he could return in the future? “Formula 1 is constantly changing,” the 37-year-old responded. “The technology, the engines, the rules, the circuits. Once you're out of it, you're out.” Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Michael Schumacher, Ferrari In the end, the attraction of competition proved too strong and Schumacher returned for a three-year stint at Mercedes from 2010 to 2012, during which he struggled to match team-mate Nico Rosberg and scored just one podium finish while topping qualifying on his last Monaco outing. But in the Schumacher camp, one major feeling when he first retired also was relief. When asked by German network RTL what made her happy, his wife, Corinna Schumacher, replied: “That we're all going to go home healthy, that nothing happened in all these years and that we got away with just the one broken leg.” Unfortunately, while the seven-time world champion emerged unscathed from his racing career, he was severely injured in a skiing accident in December 2013. Now 55 years old, he has not been seen in public since then. item.title: Pirates Minor League Awards: Gray Top Player, Hernandez Top Pitcher
item.description: The Pirates spent the week announcing their 2026 minor-league award winners. Murf Gray was named the Honus Wagner Player of the Year and Seth Hernandez was named the Bob Friend Pitcher of the Year. Gray, who also won the Wille Stargell Slugger of the Year, skyrocketed up the system in his first professional season. The 22-year-old began the season with Low-A Bradenton and ended the year in Double-A Altoona. He combined to slash .305/.402/.567 with 27 doubles, 32 home runs and 97 RBI across three levels. Gray, who was drafted by the Pirates in the second round in 2025, led Pittsburgh’s minor league players in hits (143), home runs, RBI, slugging percentage, runs (100), extra-base hits (59) and total bases (266). Hernandez split the year between Bradenton and High-A Greensboro. The ’25 first-round draft pick combined to go 6-1 with a 2.43 ERA in 18 starts. He logged 74 innings, walked 31, struck out 118 and held opponents to a .181 batting average. Hernandez, 20, was placed on the injured list with a season-ending oblique strain on July 25. At the time he landed on the IL, the right-hander was second among all minor-league pitchers in strikeouts. Both Gray (89) and Hernandez (nine) are considered top 100 prospect by MLB Pipeline. Gray is considered the third-best third base prospect. Hernandez is ranked as the top right-hander pitcher. Other Pirates Minor-League Awards Jesus Castillo was named the Bill Mazeroski Defender of the Year. Castillo played every position other than pitcher and catcher in 2026 and committed just nine errors in 288 chances. Yordany De Los Santos won the Omar Moreno Baserunner of the Year after leading the organization with 45 stolen bases in 92 games split between Bradenton and Greensboro. Right-hander Derek Diamond was named the Kent Tekulve Reliever of the Year. Diamond went 7-0 with a 2.45 ERA and a pair of saves in 37 appearances, 29 of which were with Triple-A Indianapolis. Johan De Los Santos was named the Pirates’ rookie level player of the year. The 18-year-old combined to slash .310/.431/.434 with four triples, two home runs, 10 RBI and 26 steals in 31 FCL games before a promotion to Bradenton. Irwin Ramirez was tabbed as the Pirates’ top rookie level pitcher. The right-hander went 1-1 with a 3.67 ERA in eight starts in the Florida Complex League before a promotion to Bradenton. He held opponents to a .157 batting average. The Pirates named Cecilio Beltre as the organization’s staff member of the year. He was a team development coach/mentor for the Dominican Summer League Pirates Gold team. item.title: Hornell's Mehr named Buffalo Bills Coach of the Week after big win
item.description: The Hornell/Arkport-Canaseraga football program is enjoying a strong 2026 campaign, and the Buffalo Bills have taken notice. Hornell/A-C head coach Dr. Ismail Mehr has been named one of the 2026 High School Tackle Football Coaches of the Week by the Buffalo Bills in partnership with Visa. Mehr was named the Rochester Coach of the Week by the Bills, while the Buffalo Region Coach of the Week was Chad Bartoszek of Salamanca. The weekly honor by the Bills aims to highlight football coaches' efforts on and off the field, recognizing their team's excellence on the field and their service to their communities. As part of the program, each winning coach's program will receive $1,000 from the Buffalo Bills and Visa, and each region's Coach of the Year will receive an additional $1,000 and be celebrated on the field at Highmark Stadium before the Bills vs. Jets game in January. Mehr was honored after leading the Red Raiders to a 19-13 victory over previously undefeated Alexander/Pembroke that moved Hornell/A-C to 6-1 on the season. Tyrone Buchanan sealed the win with a rushing touchdown with under five minutes left in the fourth quarter. Senior running back Matt Karr powered the running game, rushing 12 times for 147 yards and a touchdown. Mehr has been a part of Hornell football for more than two decades, noted the Bills. A 1991 Hornell High School graduate, he returned to his hometown in 2002 after completing medical school and specializing in anesthesiology. He is a board-certified anesthesiologist and medical director at UR Medicine St. James Hospital in Hornell. He began his coaching career as an assistant on the staff of legendary Hornell football coach Gene Mastin . More: Where does Hornell's Mastin now rank after new Section V wins record After years of serving as an assistant coach, Mehr took over as head coach and has led the Red Raiders for the past four seasons. "Community involvement is an important part of the Hornell football program," Mehr told the Bills. "Hornell is a small, blue-collar, hard-working community, and the football program believes strongly in giving back to the community that supports it. As a staff, we encourage our players to be active, responsible, and proud members of the community." This article originally appeared on The Evening Tribune: Hornell's Mehr named Buffalo Bills Coach of the Week after big win

item.title: ESPN analysts believe J.J. McCarthy could lead Giants to playoffs
item.description: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) and New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) during a week 6 NFL football game between New York Giants and New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. After a season-ending injury to starter Jaxson Dart, the New York Giants have been forced into taking a fluid approach to their starting quarterback situation and are now turning to their third starter of the year. Just over three weeks after trading for J.J. McCarthy, New York is officially moving him to starter and benching Jameis Winston, who relieved Dart. On Thursday’s episode of Get Up, Andrew Hawkins and Adam Schefter discussed what the move could mean not just for the Giants but for the rest of the NFC East as well. “There’s no one who is sticking out in this division, no one who’s playing well,” Hawkins said. “When you look at even the quarterback play throughout the division, I remember when Harbaugh first came, and there was so much excitement around what he could bring to this organization and Jackson Dart and everything he can bring out of him.” “If [J.J. McCarthy] plays the way he did in the 4th [quarter], [the Giants are] the favorites in the division.” @Hawk and @AdamSchefter make bold predictions for the NFC East following the Giants’ change in QB https://t.co/ijvn9Dj7IC — Get Up (@GetUpESPN) October 22, 2026 Hawkins went on to say that McCarthy producing could make the Giants the favorites in the division, which would put New York back in the playoffs. “The conversation was still, well, he’s the fourth-best quarterback in the division. Well, now that we’re this part in the season, no quarterback has really stood out, right? The Giants had their issues and concern, but I would say everything around the quarterback position, obviously, because Jaxson Dart has been out for the New York Giants, has actually looked up a lot quicker than we expected from (tight end Isaiah Likely) of the world. “Nabers looks like a top 10 wide receiver the way we expected before injury. So if you can get a little bit outta J.J., really, they’re in contention. And not only that, they’re probably, for my money, if he plays the way he did in the fourth, the favorites in the division.” Schefter pointed back to how high McCarthy was drafted as a potential indicator of what he’s capable of. “Look, if Jaxson Dart were healthy this year, they would be the favorites to win the division,” he said. “They’re now getting a quarterback who at one point was the 10th overall pick in a draft in where Caleb Williams went one, Jayden Daniels went two, and Drake Maye went three. They believe he’s got that type of ability. If they can harness that type of ability, which the Vikings were willing to just give up on it, and they have a chance to win the division and set up the franchise.” McCarthy’s first start for New York will come on Sunday against the Houston Texans. item.title: CSD escalates Tebas-Real Madrid dispute with referral to Spanish sports tribunal
item.description: CSD escalates Tebas-Real Madrid dispute with referral to Spanish sports tribunal Spain’s Higher Sports Council (CSD) has referred La Liga president Javier Tebas to the Administrative Tribunal for Sport (TAD) over comments comparing Real Madrid TV’s communication methods to propaganda used by Nazi Germany. The move follows a post published by the La Liga president on X on 16 October, with the CSD asking the independent tribunal to assess whether his remarks could constitute a serious sporting offence. Tebas, who also serves as a vice-president of the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), made the comparison while criticising Real Madrid’s media approach. The CSD has acted on its own initiative, submitting a reasoned request for the TAD to examine the matter. CSD asks TAD to assess whether Tebas breached Spanish sports law In its statement, the CSD said it had submitted the request because of Tebas’s remarks about Real Madrid. According to the council, the league president compared the club’s communication methods to the “propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Minister of Propaganda in Nazi Germany.” CSD statement on Tebas’ comments against Real Madrid. The CSD has asked the TAD to determine whether the comments show evidence of a possible breach of Article 76.4.b of Spain’s Sports Law 10/1990. The provision identifies as serious offences “notorious and public acts that undermine sporting dignity or decorum.” The referral does not establish that Tebas has committed an offence. Instead, it asks the TAD, an independent collegiate body, to assess whether the remarks fall within the scope of the legislation. CSD highlights the importance of respect in Spanish sport The council’s submission also refers to the TAD’s own legal doctrine, based on Supreme Court jurisprudence, concerning the meaning of sporting dignity and decorum. According to the CSD, these principles are linked to maintaining a civilised environment in sport, which requires mutual respect between people holding significant positions within the sporting community. The council also stressed the importance of protecting the values that allow sport to function as a space for respect, coexistence and fair play. Tebas in hot waters after controversial statements. (Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Soccerex) Tebas’s position as La Liga president and the RFEF vice-president places him among Spanish football’s most prominent administrators, making the dispute particularly significant given the institutional relationships between the league, the RFEF and Real Madrid. The CSD’s intervention moves the controversy beyond a public dispute between Tebas and Real Madrid. The TAD must now assess whether the comments meet the legal threshold for a serious sporting offence, rather than simply determine whether they were inflammatory. That distinction matters: criticism of a club’s media strategy is one thing, while a potential breach of sporting regulations is another. The referral itself is not a fi

The move follows a post published by the La Liga president on X on 16 October, with the CSD asking the independent tribunal to assess whether his remarks could constitute a serious sporting offence. Tebas, who also serves as a vice-president of the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), made the comparison while criticising Real Madrid’s media approach. The CSD has acted on its own initiative, submitting a reasoned request for the TAD to examine the matter. CSD asks TAD to assess whether Tebas breached Spanish sports law In its statement, the CSD said it had submitted the request because of Tebas’s remarks about Real Madrid. According to the council, the league president compared the club’s communication methods to the “propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Minister of Propaganda in Nazi Germany.” CSD statement on Tebas’ comments against Real Madrid. The CSD has asked the TAD to determine whether the comments show evidence of a possible breach of Article 76.4.b of Spain’s Sports Law 10/1990. The provision identifies as serious offences “notorious and public acts that undermine sporting dignity or decorum.” The referral does not establish that Tebas has committed an offence. Instead, it asks the TAD, an independent collegiate body, to assess whether the remarks fall within the scope of the legislation. CSD highlights the importance of respect in Spanish sport The council’s submission also refers to the TAD’s own legal doctrine, based on Supreme Court jurisprudence, concerning the meaning of sporting dignity and decorum. According to the CSD, these principles are linked to maintaining a civilised environment in sport, which requires mutual respect between people holding significant positions within the sporting community. The council also stressed the importance of protecting the values that allow sport to function as a space for respect, coexistence and fair play. Tebas in hot waters after controversial statements. (Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Soccerex) Tebas’s position as La Liga president and the RFEF vice-president places him among Spanish football’s most prominent administrators, making the dispute particularly significant given the institutional relationships between the league, the RFEF and Real Madrid. The TAD must now assess whether the comments meet the legal threshold for a serious sporting offence, rather than simply determine whether they were inflammatory. That distinction matters: criticism of a club’s media strategy is one thing, while a potential breach of sporting regulations is another. The referral itself is not a finding of guilt, and the tribunal’s assessment will determine whether the remarks warrant disciplinary consequences.

According to Calciomercato.com , the Brazilian defender has reportedly attracted interest from Bayer Leverkusen , who are ready to explore a move to bring him to Germany during the winter transfer window. The centre-back, born in 1997, recently sparked controversy with comments about some teammates’ lack of character following the defeat to Lazio, an issue that was subsequently resolved with an apology to Luciano Spalletti . Juventus do not consider Bremer untouchable, but his departure would depend on a particularly high offer. The defender is a key member of the squad, earning around €6 million per season . Any move therefore hinges on Bayer’s willingness to meet Juventus’ financial demands, as the club have no intention of easily letting go of one of their most important players. 🤩 Milan dream of Scott, with two more midfield targets Milan are exploring potential moves to strengthen their midfield, assessing targets for January or next summer. The former can play both as a holding midfielder and an attacking midfielder, and his contract expires in 2027, a detail that could influence the English club’s valuation. Milan are monitoring the various situations without having settled on a definitive strategy: opportunities over the coming months will determine which targets they pursue. ✍️ Inter begin talks over Thuram contract extension Inter are stepping up efforts to secure Marcus Thuram ’s long-term future. The French striker’s contract expires in 2028, but both sides want to begin talks now over an extension. According to TMW , initial contacts have been positive, paving the way for formal negotiations. The aim is to agree a deal running until 2030 , strengthening the bond between Inter and one of their key attacking players. Talks will continue over the coming weeks, with both sides keen to reach an agreement quickly. Their shared desire to continue together is an important first step towards a new deal. 🙅‍♂️ Napoli, ADL: "I’m not selling! I turned down €3.5 billion" Aurelio De Laurentiis has dismissed rumours of a possible sale of Napoli to American businessman Matt Rizzetta . Speaking to Radio Kiss Kiss , the Napoli president ruled out any intention of selling the club: " Napoli is not for sale. I have no intention of proceeding ." De Laurentiis also explained that, if he ever decided to sell, he would prefer to hand the club over to a Neapolitan businessman rather than an American. The owner also reiterated his determination to press ahead with plans to build a new stadium, stressing that he had already rejected huge offers in the past. " Years ago, I turned down €3.5 billion from Arab buyers ," he said. As for Rizzetta, De Laurentiis confirmed that he had received an approach about a potential sale, but had replied that there was no intention of selling Napoli. 🔜 Roma: Bakola a target, but not for January Roma are keeping a close eye on Bakola , Sassuolo’s young French midfielder, who has also attracted interest from Juventus and several Premier League clubs. According to TMW , however, Sassuolo have no intention of letting him go during the winter transfer window. Having arrived from Marseille last February for close to €10 million, the French youngster has already made eight appearances across Serie A and the Coppa Italia, catching the eye of several clubs with his ability. Sassuolo see Bakola as an important player for the second half of the season and aim to keep him until at least June as they look to secure comfortable survival under Alberto Aquilani . A January move therefore looks difficult for Roma: Sassuolo’s management appear unwilling to enter negotiations during this transfer window and would prefer to postpone any decisions on the midfielder’s future until the summer. 🤕 Lazio, Gud’s return delayed! Albert Gudmundsson will have to wait a little longer before returning to action. According to Il Messaggero , the latest examinations showed that the bone callus in his right shoulder has not yet fully formed. The forward will therefore miss the first matches of November and is targeting a return after the international break. Ahead of the match against Parma, Marusic and Rovella remain unavailable, while Cancellieri is ready to return to the squad. Cataldi is also nearing a return and could rotate with Belahyane to manage workloads in midfield. 😔 Fiorentina, Antognoni regrets missing centenary celebrations Giancarlo Antognoni has reflected on his decision not to attend Fiorentina ’s centenary celebrations, organised by the Commisso family. " I do feel some regret about not going, for the fans, not for the owners ," he told Torpedone , the Autolinee Toscane podcast, explaining that past disagreements had influenced his decision. The former Fiorentina icon nevertheless stressed that he had never had any problems with Joseph Commisso or Rocco’s wife, Catherine. Antognoni also commented on the team’s current situation, calling for the squad to be given time following a turnover of 13 players. " You can’t have everything straight away with such sweeping changes," he stressed, expressing confidence in Paolo Vanoli ’s work. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Alex Pereira drops heartbreaking UFC retirement update
item.description: Alex Pereira drops heartbreaking UFC retirement update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Striving for a win, UFC star Alex Pereira might now be considering hanging up his gloves and announcing his retirement. Pereira, 39, a former UFC light heavyweight and middleweight champion, still has goals left to achieve. However, the veteran plans to retire once the results start going against him. After losing to Ciryl Gane in their Heavyweight championship fight at UFC Freedom 250 at the White House, the Brazilian is looking to make his way back by becoming the UFC’s first-ever triple champion. Pereira has lost two of his last three fights. He is next scheduled to fight Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335. A victory there could open his path to a showdown with the winner of Ciryl Gane’s title defense against Josh Hokit. However, recently, speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show, Pereira dropped an unfortunate update about his career’s future. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “You gotta learn how to see when it’s your moment and when it’s not,” Pereira said. “If one day I start losing, if things start not going too good, I don’t want to be a stepping stone for nobody to be going up. I’ll just be focusing on enjoying my time and enjoying my money. “We did a very good career plan for me, my kids, my future, my kids’ future, for the institute that I built,” he added. “We’re all settled, so I have nothing to prove anymore.” Once regarded as one of the greatest fighters under multiple weight divisions, his recent array of losses could be an indication toward him finishing his career. item.title: Bernardo Silva: “I am very happy to have scored my first goal with this jersey”
item.description: Real Madrid midfielder Bernardo Silva scored the team’s opening goal against Red Bull Leipzig, his first goal as a madridista, and talked to the club’s media after the game. “I am very happy to have won this game and scored my first goal with this jersey. It was a tough match, where I think we were much better in the second half than in the first. In the first half, we created some chances but also allowed them to approach our goal quite a bit. Thibaut was very important for us. In the second half, we controlled the game much better, and in the end, we secured a good victory. We are happy and will keep moving forward,” he said. Bernardo also explained what Mourinho wants from the midfielders. “It doesn’t matter who is on the pitch. We are a team with very aggressive and strong players in one-on-one situations, who love dribbling and making runs into space. We need to find the balance between maintaining possession, finding the forwards, and being direct. We want to play fluid football, and we are getting to know each other better and trying to improve. I think the team has improved a lot in recent games, and I’m sure it will continue to do so soon. We need to strike that balance between controlling possession and the game while also not being a boring team, staying intense and aggressive, as Real Madrid has always been. That’s difficult, and you need to be very prepared to do it well,” he added. He also talked about his role. “I keep working. I’m ready to help this club. Whether it’s one minute, five, ten, or ninety… I’ll be training well, helping the group, and the day the coach feels he needs me, I’ll be ready,” he explained.

item.title: Three Numbers Define The Braves’ Offseason Choices
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Braves stand at a crossroads this winter. The team needs to decide how to keep their ace on the mound and fix a broken lineup. Three specific numbers from the 2026 season show exactly where the pressure lies. These figures are the map for the front office. The Ace and the Rotation Depth Chris Sale posted a 196 Adjusted ERA+ in his third year with Atlanta. According to MLB.com , only Greg Maddux and Reynaldo López have ever posted a better mark for the Braves in a season with at least 25 starts. Sale threw his four-seamer at 96.1 mph on average. This was the highest velocity of his career. He did not miss a single day due to injury. The key to his success was rest. The team gave him extra days off between starts. This worked perfectly for a pitcher in his age-37 season. But the rotation behind him is shaky. According to MLB.com, the sole current members forecasted to log at least 25 starts in the coming season are Sale, Grant Holmes, and Bryce Elder. Reynaldo López has a right shoulder issue that will likely limit him. Spencer Schwellenbach faces great uncertainty with a screw in his right elbow. The Braves have young talent like Spencer Strider and AJ Smith-Shawver. But they also have questions about their health and role. If Schwellenbach and Strider are healthy, should they start or pitch out of the bullpen? The team might need to add two starters this winter to keep Sale fresh. Re-signing Tyler Mahle would be a big win. Without him, the depth could run thin. The Shortstop Hole and the Dubón Decision The offense was a major problem in 2024. The Braves received a 67 Weighted Runs Created Plus from the shortstop position. This means the production at that spot was 33 percent below league average. The team also struggled at third base, left field, and second base. But the shortstop gap is the most glaring. It might be the easiest to fix. Mauricio Dubón proved he can handle the position. When playing shortstop, Dubón produced a 115 wRC+. He also had a Fielding Run Value of +3. He showed he could be an everyday player. The question is whether to make him the starter or keep him as a versatile utility man. One year ago, the Braves landed him because the Astros did not want to pay him approximately $6 million. Keeping Dubón as the everyday shortstop makes sense. If the team moves him to other spots, they leave a huge hole at shortstop. The Braves must decide if his versatility is more valuable than his bat at shortstop. The answer seems clear based on the 115 wRC+ he posted there. Looking at the Farm System While the big league team faces tough choices, the farm system is getting better. The Braves have young stars ready to help. Eric Hartman, the team’s No. 1 prospect, hit 24 homers and stole 38 bases in 94 games for High-A Rome. He entered the year as the No. 20 prospect and finished as a Top 40 prospect. item.title: 3 Players Heat Traded Lead Bucks in Scoring in Opener
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 16: Tyler Herro #11of the Milwaukee Bucks dribbles the ball against the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on October 16, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Bucks started a new era on Wednesday night — the post-Giannis Antetokounmpo period of the franchise. It’s a painful reality to face, that the best player to ever don a Bucks uniform is gone, traded to the Miami Heat. All the Bucks can do is move forward, and they didn’t get off to a great start of that with a 128-116 loss to the Washington Wizards to open their season on Wednesday. There were positive signs, though, mostly coming from the players they got in return for Giannis. In fact, three of the trade return players were the three-leading scorers for the Bucks on Wednesday. And for what it’s worth, the Heat lost their opener to, falling to the Minnesota Timberwolves . So improvements can be made all around. Tyler Herro Debut Tyler Herro is a Milwaukee-native, so it’s got to be special for him to get to play for the Bucks. Wednesday’s game was on the road, not yet home cooking for Herro, but he did lead Milwaukee in scoring. Herro put up 24 points on 9-for-21 from the floor, including 4-for-11 from 3, while making both his attempted foul shots. Herro added nine assists, two rebounds and a steal while turning the ball over four times. He’s going to have to lead the Bucks in scoring most nights to have a chance. Jaime Jaquez The forward Jaime Jaquez had a great Bucks debut after coming over in the Giannis trade. He put up 22 points on 8-for-12 from the field, including 1-for-3 from 3, and made 5-of-6 free throws. Jaquez also had seven rebounds and two assists while turning it over twice. He was the only member of the Bucks without a negative plus-minus (his was actually 0). Kasparas Jakucionis Jakucionis was just drafted in 2025, but he had a great start for the Bucks after the trade. He put up 15 points on 4-for-7 shooting, including 1-for-3 from 3, while making all six of his foul shots. Jakucionis added three rebounds and three assists with one block and one turnover. Kel’el Ware Ware was the quietest player to have arrived in the Giannis trade. He got 14 minutes off the bench and put up seven points with three rebounds, one assist, one steal and one turnover. Ware was 3-for-6 from the floor, but 0-for-2 from 3 and 1-for-3 from the foul line. It could be tough for Ware to play much more in the early going with Jaquez, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner all in the starting lineup, and on Wednesday, Ousmane Dieng got more minutes off the bench, too. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post 3 Players Heat Traded Lead Bucks in Scoring in Opener appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? FIFA responds to retracted report over compensation
item.description: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? FIFA responds to retracted report over compensation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Editor's note: this story was originally published on October 13 with information from a report by The Times which has since been retracted, as reflected in the update on October 21. Ever since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this past summer, the heat has been on Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president. The whirlwind began when Infantino had proposed selling shares of the World Cup to private equity investors, which sent fans and fellow executives into a frenzy. This scandal resulted in Infantino's position being called into question, and created a tense atmosphere in the lead-up to the upcoming FIFA presidential elections to come next spring. Now, Infantino has once again been placed in the spotlight after a report — which has since been retracted — claimed he was being paid extra compensation in addition to what FIFA disclosed publicly in its 2025 annual report. However, that report has since been retracted, sparking a heavy response from FIFA. MORE: Ranking the top candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Gianni Infantino salary as FIFA president FIFA has committed to publishing president Gianni Infantino's salary each year in its annual report, declaring his compensation in the company's yearly release. For the 2025 calendar year, Infantino was paid 4.8 million Swiss Francs (CHF), or $5.76 million in gross salary, according to FIFA's annual compensation report . This is broken down into 2.6 million CHF in base salary, and 2.2 million CHF in bonuses. Report about undisclosed payment to FIFA president is retracted According to a report by Martyn Ziegler of The Times , which has since been publicly retracted, Gianni Infantino was paid additionally on top of his disclosed salary by FIFA. The report cites 2024 U.S. tax filings by FIFA which show that Infantino was given $1.76 million by FWC2026, the company FIFA set up to run the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States this past summer. U.S.-based non-profits must fill out IRS form 990, on which FIFA disclosed to the U.S. government payments by FWC2026 to Infantino as well as FIFA General Secretary Matias Graffstrom, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, and a number of other executives involved in the tournament's production. This payment came on top of his regularly reported compensation, and was not publicly disclosed in FIFA's financial filings in their annual report. However, this report was officially retracted on October 20 by The Times who conceded that FIFA's report did not disclose this additional income because Swiss tax law rules do not count expense and reimbursement payments as compensation with regards to filings and reportings by non-profits. item.content:encoded: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? FIFA responds to retracted report over compensation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Editor's note: this story was originally published on October 13 with information from a report by The Times which has since been retracted, as reflected in the update on October 21. Ever since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this past summer, the heat has been on Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president. The whirlwind began when Infantino had proposed selling shares of the World Cup to private equity investors, which sent fans and fellow executives into a frenzy. This scandal resulted in Infantino's position being called into question, and created a tense atmosphere in the lead-up to the upcoming FIFA presidential elections to come next spring. Now, Infantino has once again been placed in the spotlight after a report — which has since been retracted — claimed he was being paid extra compensation in addition to what FIFA disclosed publicly in its 2025 annual report. However, that report has since been retracted, sparking a heavy response from FIFA. MORE: Ranking the top candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Gianni Infantino salary as FIFA president FIFA has committed to publishing president Gianni Infantino's salary each year in its annual report, declaring his compensation in the company's yearly release. For the 2025 calendar year, Infantino was paid 4.8 million Swiss Francs (CHF), or $5.76 million in gross salary, according to FIFA's annual compensation report . This is broken down into 2.6 million CHF in base salary, and 2.2 million CHF in bonuses. Report about undisclosed payment to FIFA president is retracted According to a report by Martyn Ziegler of The Times , which has since been publicly retracted, Gianni Infantino was paid additionally on top of his disclosed salary by FIFA. The report cites 2024 U.S. tax filings by FIFA which show that Infantino was given $1.76 million by FWC2026, the company FIFA set up to run the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States this past summer. U.S.-based non-profits must fill out IRS form 990, on which FIFA disclosed to the U.S. government payments by FWC2026 to Infantino as well as FIFA General Secretary Matias Graffstrom, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, and a number of other executives involved in the tournament's production. This payment came on top of his regularly reported compensation, and was not publicly disclosed in FIFA's financial filings in their annual report. However, this report was officially retracted on October 20 by The Times who conceded that FIFA's report did not disclose this additional income because Swiss tax law rules do not count expense and reimbursement payments as compensation with regards to filings and reportings by non-profits. They also acknowledged that claims regarding a Miami property purchase were false. FIFA assert that Infantino's payments from FWC2026 were not part of his regular salary or compensation, and therefore were not required to be disclosed in their annual report by Swiss tax law, and therefore, while included in the U.S. tax filings, were not required to be publicly announced. FIFA & FIFA PRESIDENT RECEIVES APOLOGY FROM ‘THE TIMES’ FIFA takes note of an apology published today by The Times following an inaccurate and damaging report: On 13 October 2026 (Sport), we reported that Gianni Infantino received a "second salary" from Fifa, which Fifa had failed to disclose. This is incorrect. There was no “second salary.” Regulations do not require Fifa to include expenses and reimbursements received by Mr Infantino in its annual report as they are not considered "compensation" under Swiss reporting requirements. We also accept Mr Infantino did not purchase a property in Miami at a suspected undervalue as we reported and neither he nor his family are the legal or beneficial owners of Shadi LLC and have no control over that company, as we suggested. We are happy to make these corrections and apologise to Mr Infantino and Fifa for the errors. As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA urges the media to act responsibly and carefully verify all sourcing to prevent the publication and subsequent reproduction of false and defamatory information. FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate, misleading, or totally false, as in this case, FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously. — FIFA Media (@fifamedia) October 20, 2026 Following the retraction, FIFA acknowledged the apology they received from The Times and warned there was a "concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President."

item.title: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel Issues Warning About Bears’ Ben Johnson Before TNF
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Mike Vrabel of the New England Patriots reacts after a play against the Buffalo Bills during the second quarter at Highmark Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears reacts during the second quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 and Kalif Raymond #14 of the Chicago Bears celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The New England Patriots have much to ponder ahead of Thursday night’s matchup against the Chicago Bears. And head coach Mike Vrabel knows that preparing for Ben Johnson’s offense is rarely clear-cut. The Bears coach has a reputation for keeping defenses guessing with atypical formations, plus aggressive fourth-down decisions and a trick play thrown in. Vrabel is wary of that unpredictability marching into Soldier Field. Vrabel Points to Johnson’s Unpredictable Play-Calling Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 04: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears reacts during the second quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) Asked about the biggest challenge of preparing for Johnson, Vrabel pointed to the sheer number of possibilities Chicago puts out there. “There’s a lot of volume. They do a lot of things well, and you’ll have to be prepared for some unscouted looks,” Vrabel said during his October 21 press conference . “But he stays aggressive. He has a lot of faith in those guys on fourth down. He marries up formations and motions.” Seeing something unexpected from Johnson can happen even with limited preparation time. When asked whether the Bears HC might unveil an unscouted look on a Thursday night, Vrabel remembered an example. “They handed the ball to the left tackle, who was going to throw a pass on four days in Detroit, so probably,” he said. Vrabel was referencing a trick play involving Penei Sewell during the Detroit Lions ‘ Thanksgiving matchup against Chicago in November 2024. Sewell took a reverse and prepared to throw the football before taking a sack when nobody was open. The play lost yardage, but it illustrated Johnson’s willingness to put the ball in unanticipated hands. The former Lions offensive coordinator has that creativity in (and before) his second season leading Chicago. Against the Atlanta Falcons on October 18, Johnson’s offense successfully executed a hook-and-ladder involving Caleb Williams , Rome Odunze and Roschon Johnson . The play gained 12 yards and moved the chains. Patriots Go to War With Bears’ Offense Getty ATLANTA

(Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 and Kalif Raymond #14 of the Chicago Bears celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. He has a lot of faith in those guys on fourth down. He marries up formations and motions.” Seeing something unexpected from Johnson can happen even with limited preparation time. When asked whether the Bears HC might unveil an unscouted look on a Thursday night, Vrabel remembered an example. “They handed the ball to the left tackle, who was going to throw a pass on four days in Detroit, so probably,” he said. The former Lions offensive coordinator has that creativity in (and before) his second season leading Chicago. Against the Atlanta Falcons on October 18, Johnson’s offense successfully executed a hook-and-ladder involving Caleb Williams , Rome Odunze and Roschon Johnson . (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) The trick plays are only part of what Vrabel’s defense will need to meet with tact. Chicago has also demonstrated an ability to sustain possessions and control the tempo of games. According to Patriots.com’s Evan Lazar , the Bears are averaging 73.2 offensive plays per game while their opponents are running just 50.2. That disparity has allowed Johnson’s offense to dictate the pace, while making it tougher for opposing quarterbacks to get the ball in their hands. Chicago also leads the NFL with 15 fourth-down attempts, reflecting the aggressive approach Vrabel highlighted. Since this Patriots team is bogged down by injuries throughout its roster, notably along the offensive line, those longer possessions pose an obstacle. Vrabel stressed turning the tables. “That’s the challenge, is being able to flip the script a little bit, not let them run 73 plays and only have to defend 50,” he said. New England enters the contest with a 4-2 record, matching Chicago’s mark through six games. item.title: Rangers Daily: Sully pushes back; Crazy Ottawa return for Brady Tkachuk
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mike Sullivan apparently heard the outside noise and wanted to set the record straight about certain poor underlying metrics for the New York Rangers defensemen so far this season. As reported in several spaces, including here in a recent article published by Tom Castro , the Rangers spend a lot of time defending, are being out-chanced, and have a mediocre expected goal share — collectively as a team, and individually by player. Castro pointed these things out, backed up by underlying metrics from Natural Stat Trick , and stated that it’s something the Rangers should have some level of concern about. Of course, the Rangers are 7-3-1 to start the season and certainly pass the eye test in most areas of their play. Their defensive zone exits are much crisper and cleaner, and the support and structure sure appear better than in previous seasons. A big part of that is that New York works much better now in five-man groups with the forwards much more dedicated to playing a 200-foot game, which Castro rightly pointed out. But Sullivan also correctly argued that one can’t simply look at any one stat or underlying metric in a vacuum to form a complete opinion. “When you start looking at metrics and things of that nature, context is really important. If you don’t understand context, it’s hard for you to interpret data the right way,” the Rangers coach said Wednesday . “So for example, if there’s a defense pair or a line combination that gets a lot of defensive-zone starts against the other team’s top players, they’re probably going to be on the ice for some chances against. But they might limit the quality of the chance or the quantity of the chances of the other team’s top players, and they keep them off the board, and we have success because of it. Their metrics might not look positive, but the value is they help us win.” Specifically speaking about the team’s new second defense pairing of Marcus Pettersson and Sean Durzi , there’s no question the Rangers are much better off with those two veterans in that role than any combinations they put together in recent years. I pointed to that is the Rangers Daily column on Wednesday. “When you look at multiple data points, it gives you a little bit of a better picture of what that context is or what it looks like. So, we believe Marcus and ‘Durz’ have given us pretty good minutes,” Sullivan explained. “Some nights they’ve been better than others, without a doubt. But I also think there’s more to it than (the analytics).” Fair enough. Analytics are important. So, too, are results, the eye test, the human element. That’s why the Yankees bringing back the analytics-driven Aaron Boone as manager draws so much criticism from fans and reporters alike, because it’s so one-sided how he runs that team and goes about making his decisions. Sully appears to have a good balance of both in how he oversees the Rangers. New York Rangers news and analysis Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IM

New York Rangers news and analysis Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With stick taps to longtime AHL beat reporter Patrick Williams, we take a dive into explaining Dylan Garand’s success with the Rangers , focusing more on what’s between his ears than the technical aspects. Tomas Chrenko heating up in Slovakia tops Steven Voogel’s report on Rangers prospects playing in Europe. This is pretty cool: in the most recent NCAA men’s hockey rankings, the top five teams each has one Rangers prospect playing on it , including No. 1- ranked Michigan, with forward Malcolm Spence . Keith Yandle shared a story on a recent podcast about why he opted to reject a contract offer to remain with the Rangers back in the summer of 2016. NHL news and rumors Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect TSN : It was quite the theater in Ottawa on Wednesday night, when Senators fan brought their A Game and directed a heaping dose of vitriol at former captain Brady Tkachuk in his return after forcing a trade to the Florida Panthers this past offseason. Oh, and the Senators won 5-1, despite Brady scoring the first goal of the contest. Sportsnet : Nice job by the Sportsnet crew putting together this highlight video showcasing the creative chants from the Senators fans directed at Brady Tkachuk in his return to Canadian Tire Cnetre. Florida Hockey Now : George Richards has this take from the Panthers side of an eventful night in Ottawa. TSN : Some potentially bad news in an otherwise excellent night for the Senators: No. 1 goalie Linus Ullmark left the game in the third period with a lower-body injury. New Jersey Hockey Now : James Nichols takes a deep dive into what it would take for the Devils to trade for Dylan Larkin and fit him under their salary cap. Pittsburgh Hockey Now: Penguins coach Dan Muse said in a radio interview that forward Ben Kindel is doing better and could return to Pittsburgh by time you read this following a medical episode that forced the team charter to return to Salt Lake City so that he could be rushed to a local hospital there. Sportsnet : Some really good news for the defending Stanley Cup champs as talented forward Seth Jarvis will make his season debut for the Carolina Hurricanes against the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday following offseason shoulder surgery. Boston Hockey Now : Jack Studley reports on the Bruins signing forward Marat Khusnutdinov to a three-year, $11.85 million contract extension. Sportsnet : First-year Vancouver Canucks general manager Ryan Johnson is trying to hold things together and preaches patience as his team wobbles through an eight-game losing streak. item.title: ‘Never seen this happen’ – Ben Roethlisberger has spotted ‘unusual’ Aaron Rodgers issue
item.description: Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are heading to Paris, France, where they will be facing the New Orleans Saints with the opportunity to extend their record to 5-2 on the season. Despite there being some shaky moments in the Steelers’ opening six games of the year but there have also been some really encouraging performances. The win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday was far from convincing but it was yet another strong showing from Aaron Rodgers. The 42-year-old quarterback threw for 253 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday in Florida but there were some moments that Ben Roethlisberger did not totally love. Rodgers and Mike McCarthy’s relationship has been put to the test during the early stages of the season and Roethlisberger is still not convinced the pair are always on the same page. Ben Roethlisberger pinpoints ‘unusual’ Aaron Rodgers issue for the Steelers Earlier in the season, Rodgers was spotted by the broadcast cameras shouting at his head coach as he demanded the play call quicker. The play calls are seemingly still proving a slight issue which is leaving Roethlisberger baffled given the pair’s long-standing relationship. “It’s not easy for Aaron, and it just seems unusual again that those guys, like McCarthy and Rodgers, know each other so well. They’ve been around each other for so long. You’ve never seen this happen in the past, so why is it? Is there an issue now?” Roethlisberger said on the Footbahlin podcast. “Maybe McCarthy hurt his foot, and he was dealing with the pain. I don’t know, or his ankle, or whatever he’s got going on. It just seems unusual for a Rodgers-led team, for him not to have even more time up there to do his thing. It’s just what we’ve seen in the past from him and his offence.” It took the Steelers’ offence until the final quarter of the game as they scored 16 of their 19 points in regular time in the fourth quarter. Rodgers was able to force overtime but the Steelers walk away from the game looking far from convincing. Despite their history together, there just seems to be something slightly off between Rodgers and McCarthy this season. Although that is not to say their relationship has worsened but the pair do not appear to be singing of the same hymn sheet. item.title: “Could Not Disagree More”: Robert Saleh Gets No Support from FOX Radio Host After Seemingly Downplaying Jordan Elliott’s Firearm Incident
item.description: Robert Saleh © Imagn Robert Saleh attempted to give an explanation about the situation around Jordan Elliott after the defensive tackle was released by the Tennessee Titans following an incident involving a firearm, but it appears not everyone is on board with the head coach’s words. FOX Sports host Rob Parker has hit out at Saleh for his comments regarding the incident, suggesting that there is no way that a positive word can be said about the entire fiasco. “I could not disagree more with Robert Saleh…if you are going to go to bat for that young man why is he off the team then? Why don’t you get him the help and rehabilitate him and give him another opportunity?” Parker said on FOX Sports Radio. “To act like someone going to their car to get a gun is not criminal, is not scary, to put everybody at risk, and to make this impassioned plea…and that we shouldn’t have a knee-jerk reaction…really?” Robert Saleh’s Explanation of the Jordan Elliott Incident Robert Saleh attempted to cast Jordan Elliott in some positive light after the entire incident had unfolded at the Titans facility. “Unfortunately, rules are rules with regard to guns on property, and sometimes it’s far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they’re down,” he said, as also reported by the National Herald. “He’s a good man. Made a terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act,” Saleh went on. “He’s never committed a crime in his entire life and he pulled a gun, in the parking lot.” Regardless of Saleh’s explanation, the Titans have already made the decision to release the player and it remains to be seen whether any other team in the future will take a chance on Jordan Elliott. item.title: Patrick Mahomes shares how Kenneth Walker is really feeling about Seattle Seahawks reunion
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Kenneth Walker III has been perhaps the most impressive running back in the entire league through the opening weeks of the season following his move to the Kansas City Chiefs. The Super Bowl MVP left the Seattle Seahawks earlier in the year having only just won a ring under head coach Mike Macdonald. Walker has ensured the Seahawks regretted the decision not to go all out to keep him after he’s racked up 665 rushing yards and eight total touchdowns on the season. As Walker continues to impress with the Chiefs, the Seahawks have been left struggling beyond belief at the running back position. Injuries and players failing to secure the ball has almost eliminated the run game in the Pacific Northwest. Having failed to offer Walker a contract earlier in the year, the running back is now preparing to face his former team for the first time since departing in March. What Kenneth Walker is thinking about his reunion with the Seattle Seahawks Salt has certainly been rubbed into the wounds of those back in Seattle as Walker’s incredible performances highlight their deficiencies in the running back position. Although Zach Charbonnet could return this weekend, not having Walker playing in blue has been a massive blow for the Seahawks. “I know it’s going to be a special moment for him… You get to go back to a place where you built your career and won a Super Bowl… at the end of the day, you’ve got to win a football game… He knows we’ve got his back,” said Patrick Mahomes when asked about Walker’s return. Walker has already made his feelings clear on general manager John Schneider’s decision not to sign him earlier in the year. After winning the Super Bowl, Walker did not return to Seattle for the team’s ring ceremony which was a real indicator of his frustrations. The Seahawks have been one of the best run defences in the league over the last two seasons but they have rarely faced a back just as dominant as Walker is playing right now. With just one game returning less than 100 rushing yards this season, Seattle certainly has a difference maker to keep quiet.
