item.title: Giants Announce Signing of Former Eagles Player Days Before Texans Game
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Head coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants takes the field prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty On Sunday, the 3-2-1 New York Giants will take on the 2-4 Houston Texans at NRG Stadium. The New York Giants remain atop the NFC East, which has been perhaps the most disappointing division in the NFL. However, that presents the Giants with an opportunity to win the division for the first time since 2011. After Week 6’s loss against the New Orleans Saints, it has been a news-filled week for the New York Giants. The team made a quarterback change, replacing Jameis Winston with J.J. McCarthy, and also released running back Najee Harris, who was the team’s starter against the Saints. In the middle of that, the Giants also announced a roster move as they signed an offensive lineman, who started his career with the Philadelphia Eagles. New York Giants Sign Offensive Lineman View this post on Instagram After Wednesday’s practice session, New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh announced a signing, saying, “We also acquired a player from the Colts, Josh Sills, an offensive lineman, who we took off the practice squad, so he’ll be on our roster going forward.” Regarding the move, Giants Wire’s Dan Benton wrote: “The move comes as the Giants deal with injuries to their top three offensive tackles, all of whom missed Wednesday’s session. Left tackle Andrew Thomas has managed a groin issue since Week 2 and has played sparingly at times. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor is dealing with a calf injury that forced him to miss last week’s game against the New Orleans Saints. Marcus Mbow appeared to suffer an injury late in that contest.” Benton added of Sills’s trajectory: “Sills, 28, is a 6-foot-6, 325-pound lineman who went undrafted in 2022 after playing at West Virginia and Oklahoma State, where he earned first-team All-Big 12 honors in consecutive seasons. He signed with the Philadelphia Eagles as a free agent, appeared in one game as a rookie, and was claimed by the Colts in 2023. Across his career, he has played in 21 games without a start, logging 41 offensive snaps while contributing more extensively on special teams. Though primarily used as a guard, his size and experience provide additional depth as the Giants navigate their tackle situation.” Giants’ Injury Status Hopefully Sills’ signing does not mean the Giants will be without any of their top offensive linemen. Perhaps the most worrying aspect of New York’s injuries is Andrew Thomas’s status. Thomas has been absent from a majority of New York’s practice sessions this season and did not return during the Giants’ game against the Saints despite clearing concussion protocol. item.title: Jersey ensure World Cup progress after PNG win
item.description: Zak Tribe’s 150 was his highest score for Jersey [Jersey Cricket/ICC] Jersey ensured progression to the next round of qualifying for the Cricket World Cup after a record-breaking win over Papua New Guinea in Nairobi. Jersey scored 347-5 - their highest-ever tally in a 50-over game - as Zak Tribe's 150 became his biggest total for the island. In reply Papua New Guinea could only muster 175 all out from 36.5 overs as Ben Ward took 5-49 as the island side won by 172 runs. The victory means Jersey are guaranteed a top two finish in ICC Challenge League A, and with it a place in December's ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifier play-off in Nepal. Jonty Jenner hit 72 off just 23 balls for Jersey [Jersey Cricket/ICC] Having lost opener Harrison Carlyon for 18 off 19 balls after four overs, Jersey's star batter Asa Tribe made his return to the island side. The Glamorgan and England Lions player had not played for Jersey since last summer, but he had a tricky return. He and Josh Lawrenson put on just 12 runs in the first six overs of their partnership before Tribe eventually went for 23 off 29 balls when he was bowled by Aue Oru in the first ball of the 13th over to leave Jersey on 58-2. His brother replaced him, and with opener Lawrenson set about a disciplined third-wicket partnership - Tribe reached his half-century off 58 balls while Lawrenson's 50 came off 74 balls. Tribe brought up his century with a huge six on his 105th ball as he and Lawrenson put on a match-defining 165-run stand before Lawrenson was bowled by John Kariko for 72 off 95 balls. Any restrictions to Jersey's batting were removed after Lawrenson's departure as big-hitting Jonty Jenner replaced him and hit a 17-ball half-century, ending on 72 from 23 balls that included nine sixes and two fours as he and Tribe put on 113 runs for the fourth wicket inside just 6.4 overs. Tribe went on to hit five sixes and 11 fours as he ended on 150 off 129 balls - his total has only been bettered by brother Asa who scored 175 in a win over Qatar last summer. Tribe aims to help Jersey despite England ambitions Tribe in Jersey team for World Cup Challenge final round In reply Carlyon struck in the first over as he claimed the wicket of Doko Rupa for a duck to leave the Papuans on 3-1. But Sese Bau and Lega Siaka put on 46 for the second wicket before George Richardson bowled the dangerous Bau for 22 as his side moved on to 48-2 from 10 overs. Ben Ward claimed Siaka for 39 before bowling Patrick Nou for 14 and captain Assad Vala for 4 as Papua new Guinea were reduced to 86-5 off 19.2 overs. Ward went on to claim two more wickets as they moved on to 101-8 off 24.2 overs. But Kabis Morea and Alei Nao provided some stiff ninth-wicket resistance with a partnership of 64 before Nao was bowled by Charles Perchard for 32. Morea went on to make 40 before being trapped lbw by Lawrenson as Papua New Guinea ended on 175 all out from 36.5 overs.

item.title: Report: Nagelsmann a candidate for Man Utd coaching job
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Then Germany Coach Julian Nagelsmann applauds during the 2026 FIFA World Cup Group E soccer match between Germany and Ivory Coast at Toronto Stadium. (is associated with: «Report: Nagelsmann a candidate for Man Utd coaching job») Tom Weller/dpa Former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann is reportedly a candidate at Manchester United should Michael Carrick have to go in the wake of poor results. The Daily Telegraph said on Thursday that Nagelsmann is top of the list of candidates at Old Trafford. The report said that Nagelsmann was ready for talks in the case of an offer. Pressure on Carrick grew when United crashed 4-1 at Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. They have one victory from three games in the elite event, and also only one, from seven matches in the Premier League in what is their worst start in England since 1986. United next play against Bournemouth on Sunday. Nagelsmann resigned as Germany coach in July after a disappointing round of 32 exit against Paraguay at the World Cup. He previously coached Bundesliga clubs Hoffenheim, RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich. There has also been speculation about a Leipzig return after they have started modestly into the season under new coach Martin Demichelis. Nagelsmann has been linked with a move to England in the past as well, but a move to Chelsea or Tottenham Hotspur didn't happen. Other United candidates reportedly are former Italy coach Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe, who left Newcastle United at the end of July.

item.title: Seahawks Get Blunt Take on Kenneth Walker III Decision Before Chiefs Game
item.description: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks are facing the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7, which means conversations over the team’s decision to let Kenneth Walker III leave as a free agent are at the forefront. Walker was coming off an MVP performance in Super Bowl LX, making it a difficult decision for Seattle to let him walk. However, the Seahawks likely wanted to allocate that money toward retaining other players. Nonetheless, the running back would land a three-year, $43.05 million contract with the Kansas City Chiefs, and so far he’s been worth every single dollar and more. Walker has played 241 total snaps for the Chiefs, leading to a 90.8 overall PFF grade . Moreover, the Chiefs star has carried the ball 106 times for 665 rushing yards and six touchdowns. Walker has also forced 41 missed tackles as a runner while averaging 4.4 yards after contact per attempt. Meanwhile, in the passing game, he has caught 14 passes on 19 targets for 95 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Former Seahawks tight end and TSN NFL analyst Luke Willson shared his thoughts on whether Seattle made a mistake allowing Walker to leave. “It certainly seems like it’s a massive one, but I do think we’re a little too quick to completely stamp that as a mistake,” Wilson said on an Oct. 21 appearance on TSN . “The reason being here is you look at Seattle. Some of the money they spent on offense this offseason went toward Rashid Shaheed , also a special teams guy, and that offense in Seattle has struggled mightily. So, that being said, I don’t think they’re completely cooked yet, as we like to use that term.” Seahawks Have to Get Two Key Players Going Moreover, Wilson believes that if the Seahawks can get Shaheed and Jadarian Price , once he returns from injury, going, then the conversation around whether they made a mistake with Walker will begin to quiet down. “If they can get Shaheed going, and I say the new offensive coordinator, Brian Fleury, some of that whole question about whether we should have Kenneth Walker, I think, starts to dissipate. The next thing is the rookie, Jadarian Price. He comes in as a first-round pick. It hasn’t really worked out in the first few games. He also sustained an injury and hasn’t played. “I think Seahawks fans need to give this guy a little bit of grace before we say, ‘Okay, this is a terrible mistake. We should have had Kenneth Walker.’ Don’t get me wrong, in Andy Reid’s offense with Patrick Mahomes , Kenneth Walker has been out of this world. He looks like the Offensive Player of the Year thus far, but it’s still very early and it’s not just a direct comparison here.” Seattle Receives Candid Message on QB Situation While the Seahawks will be judged on whether they made a mistake allowing Walker to leave, they have other issues given their two-game losing streak, and one of them is the play at QB. Despite conversation regarding the Seahawks’ QB position and whether Darnold should remain the starter, Seattle Sports’ Michael Bumpus believes that making a change won’t fix the team’s issues. “This isn’t Madden,” Bumpus said in an Oct. 16 video from Seattle Sports . “People talk as if they don’t know what they’re doing. How quickly do you jump ship from a team that brought you a Super Bowl? Sam, a Super Bowl-winning quarterback, is turning the ball over. Yes, he is. He’s turning the ball over. Just inserting another quarterback is not going to fix it.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Seahawks Get Blunt Take on Kenneth Walker III Decision Before Chiefs Game appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Searle rejected France move to push on at Tigers
item.description: Billy Searle scored 15 points in his only appearance for England A in a 52-14 win against Ireland in February [Getty Images] Leicester Tigers fly-half Billy Searle turned down a potential return to France to "push his game on" at Welford Road and stay on the radar for full England honours in the near future. Searle, 30, agreed a new three-year deal in September , having joined Tigers from French club Agen for the start of 2025-26. The former Bristol, Wasps and Worcester Warriors stand-off has had three spells playing French rugby in his career - a short stint at Toulouse in 2022, and with second-tier Biarritz and Agen - before moving back to England. But he told BBC Radio Leicester, once the details of his new Leicester contract were ironed out, staying with Geoff Parling's Tigers was the only thing he wanted. "I've loved it. I've always felt like it's really suited my game and the fans have taken to me really well," Searle said. "So it was an easy decision. It took longer than we probably wanted it from both sides, but that's just part of negotiations. "When we got that sorted before the season started that was a big positive for me. Geoff made it clear they want to keep me, I made it clear to the club my priority would be to stay. "I had interest in France but I made it clear I wanted to stay. I've moved around quite a bit in my career and I really felt like I found my feet here." He scored five tries but could only think of a sixth There can be 'beauty' in low scores - Tigers boss Parling Leicester fly-half Searle agrees new contract Searle added that extending his Tigers career will enable him to "be in an environment where I feel I'm getting better". "I'm pushing on and feel like I'm playing some of my best rugby," he added. "My main motivation was to be settled here and lead this team forward and really push my game on." Searle has also not given up hope of adding a first senior cap to his England A appearance against Ireland in February - which would have not been possible had he moved back to France. "I think it's always in the back of your mind - it's one of the reasons I came back, hopefully pushing into that bracket," he said. "I had a few conversations with [head coach] Steve [Borthwick] - just 'off the books' conversations about my game. So it's always in the back of your mind. "I know [2027] that's a World Cup year, s there's no reason why if you can't go well and keep pushing the door you might get an opportunity." item.title: Kenny Wallace Asked Fans Not to Make Fun of Him. Then He Pitched His Idea for Women Racers
item.description: Kenny Wallace named three of the six women who raced the ARCA Menards Series West round at Phoenix Raceway on Oct. 17, then told his viewers, "Now that's as far as I could remember." The one he left out, Mia Lovell, finished eighth. The line is from a "Coffee with Kenny" episode Wallace posted to his YouTube channel and his X account the next morning under the title "Should ARCA Be The Women's Series?" He filmed it in a $104-a-night hotel room in Lincoln, Illinois, where he was entered in the DIRTcar Fall Nationals at Lincoln Speedway. The part about women runs roughly three minutes of a video that is close to 11 minutes long. Most of the rest is about money in dirt racing. After asking viewers not to make fun of him, Wallace made the pitch: "Maybe that's the ladies series. Maybe ARCA is perfect to get them going." His reasoning was that the next rungs are too steep. "Truck series, the O'Reilly series, hey, you might as well be in Cup," he said, calling the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series "a big step for these ladies." What the results show ARCA's official results list 27 starters in the Desert Diamond Casino West Valley 100. Taylor Reimer finished second in Pinnacle Racing Group's No. 82 Chevrolet, Hailie Deegan was sixth, Lovell eighth and Jade Avedisian ninth. Taylor Mayhew (13th) and Dystany Spurlock (14th) also finished on the lead lap, as did all six women. Reimer took the lead from Max Reaves before the halfway break and got it back briefly in traffic near the end, according to ARCA's race report . Reaves won when rain ended the race under caution after an overtime restart, giving Joe Gibbs Racing a win in its last ARCA event before the team closes the program. ARCA called second place Reimer's best finish in its competition so far. Wallace said he found out how the race went on X, a site he described as "totally toxic" before admitting it is good for highlights. A minute later he added, "Remember, I'm a girl dad. I have three daughters." Phoenix Raceway during a 2025 race (representative image, not from the Oct. 17 ARCA West event). Photo: Brycenrichter via Wikimedia Commons, CC0 The ladder Deegan already climbed The sixth-place finisher has already done the route Wallace describes, in both directions. Racing-Reference's records show Deegan made 70 starts across ARCA's main, East and West series from 2018 to 2020, including a full 2020 ARCA season in which she ran 17 top-10s in 20 races and finished third in points. Then she moved up. Deegan made 69 Truck Series starts from 2020 to 2023 with five top-10s and a best championship finish of 17th. She added 18 starts in what is now the O'Reilly series, 17 of them in AM Racing's No. 15 Ford in 2024, without a top-10. Hailie Deegan in AM Racing's No. 15 Ford at Sonoma Raceway during her 2024 Xfinity Series season. item.content:encoded: Kenny Wallace named three of the six women who raced the ARCA Menards Series West round at Phoenix Raceway on Oct. 17, then told his viewers, "Now that's as far as I could remember." The one he left out, Mia Lovell, finished eighth. The line is from a "Coffee with Kenny" episode Wallace posted to his YouTube channel and his X account the next morning under the title "Should ARCA Be The Women's Series?" He filmed it in a $104-a-night hotel room in Lincoln, Illinois, where he was entered in the DIRTcar Fall Nationals at Lincoln Speedway. The part about women runs roughly three minutes of a video that is close to 11 minutes long. Most of the rest is about money in dirt racing. After asking viewers not to make fun of him, Wallace made the pitch: "Maybe that's the ladies series. Maybe ARCA is perfect to get them going." His reasoning was that the next rungs are too steep. "Truck series, the O'Reilly series, hey, you might as well be in Cup," he said, calling the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series "a big step for these ladies." What the results show ARCA's official results list 27 starters in the Desert Diamond Casino West Valley 100. Taylor Reimer finished second in Pinnacle Racing Group's No. 82 Chevrolet, Hailie Deegan was sixth, Lovell eighth and Jade Avedisian ninth. Taylor Mayhew (13th) and Dystany Spurlock (14th) also finished on the lead lap, as did all six women. Reimer took the lead from Max Reaves before the halfway break and got it back briefly in traffic near the end, according to ARCA's race report . Reaves won when rain ended the race under caution after an overtime restart, giving Joe Gibbs Racing a win in its last ARCA event before the team closes the program. ARCA called second place Reimer's best finish in its competition so far. Wallace said he found out how the race went on X, a site he described as "totally toxic" before admitting it is good for highlights. A minute later he added, "Remember, I'm a girl dad. I have three daughters." Phoenix Raceway during a 2025 race (representative image, not from the Oct. 17 ARCA West event). Photo: Brycenrichter via Wikimedia Commons, CC0 The ladder Deegan already climbed The sixth-place finisher has already done the route Wallace describes, in both directions. Racing-Reference's records show Deegan made 70 starts across ARCA's main, East and West series from 2018 to 2020, including a full 2020 ARCA season in which she ran 17 top-10s in 20 races and finished third in points. Then she moved up. Deegan made 69 Truck Series starts from 2020 to 2023 with five top-10s and a best championship finish of 17th. She added 18 starts in what is now the O'Reilly series, 17 of them in AM Racing's No. 15 Ford in 2024, without a top-10. Hailie Deegan in AM Racing's No. 15 Ford at Sonoma Raceway during her 2024 Xfinity Series season. Photo: TaurusEmerald via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 This year she is back in ARCA West with Bill McAnally Racing: 12 starts, one win, eight top-10s and fourth in the standings. Her record fits the part of Wallace's argument about the size of the jump. It does not fit the idea that women racers are skipping ARCA. Deegan spent three seasons there first. Wallace's own apprenticeship was three seasons in the American Speed Association, 1986 through 1988, before a full Busch Series schedule in 1989. His niece Chrissy Wallace, his brother Mike's daughter, made seven Truck starts in 2008 and 2009 and two Nationwide Series starts in 2010. Who pays for the next step The video never mentions budgets. Denny Hamlin said this week that four out of five O'Reilly Series drivers are paying to race , and that bill lands on the 21 men in Saturday's Phoenix field the same way it lands on the six women. Sorting drivers into an ARCA "ladies series" would not change who can afford a Truck seat. Wallace has stood up for women drivers before. In February he defended Natalie Decker when a Daytona wreck turned into an online pile-on. Three months later Decker walked away from her Truck team after Dover . ARCA's standing as a place to learn stock cars reaches past racing, too. This month Tom Cruise asked NASCAR for a real ARCA start before filming Days of Thunder 2. Nobody has suggested he stay there. Wallace closed the segment by asking viewers to weigh in. By Thursday the YouTube upload had about 22,000 views and 118 comments. The X post had four replies. The ARCA West season ends Oct. 31 with the NAPA Auto Parts 150 at Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway, streaming on FloRacing at 7 p.m. PT. Deegan goes in fourth in points. Should ARCA be the place women racers stay until they are ready for Trucks, or does a "ladies series" label miss a ladder that is mostly decided by money? Sources: ARCA race report and official results, Desert Diamond Casino West Valley 100, Oct. 18, 2026; Kenny Wallace, "Should ARCA Be The Women's Series?" on YouTube and X, Oct. 18, 2026; Racing-Reference driver statistics for Hailie Deegan and Chrissy Wallace. ⚡ Read the full article on Backfire News Sign up for the Backfire Newsletter . item.title: Dolphins Trade Pitch Sends Key Starter to Super Bowl Contender
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins walks off the field following a pre season game against the New York Giants at Hard Rock Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Getty At 0-5, it would not be shocking to see the Miami Dolphins become sellers at the trade deadline. In fact, Miami has operated as a seller since before the season, as they traded key starters Jaylen Waddle and Minkah Fitzpatrick for draft capital this offseason. Additionally, they moved on from veterans such as Tyreek Hill, Tua Tagovailoa, Bradley Chubb and Darren Waller. By all means, the Dolphins are embracing a youth movement. While some of the team’s rookie players have performed well and exceeded expectations, the team still has a long way to go before being playoff contenders. As a result, Miami’s oldest non-special-teams player is becoming a potential trade target for teams looking to add a talented defensive lineman. Miami Dolphins Defensive Lineman Might Be Traded View this post on Instagram Sports Illustrated’s Matt Verderame included Miami Dolphins defensive lineman Zach Sieler among 15 players who might be traded before the deadline. Verderame wrote: “Sieler is an interesting trade chip. On one hand, he’s already 31 and he’s signed through 2029 with base salaries of $12.6 million, $15.4 million and $16.2 million, respectively. In short, he’s not cheap to acquire. Conversely, none of that money is guaranteed, and he could be traded for and then released for no dead cap charge if things don’t work out. For Miami, it makes sense to move on, but what’s the right price point? Since 2023, Sieler has 27.5 sacks.” Verderame named the playoff-contending Detroit Lions as a possible trade destination for Sieler. The Lions currently have one of the NFL’s best offenses, but have allowed the third-most points in the league this season. Adding Sieler would certainly improve that area of the ball for Detroit. Sieler is currently Miami’s longest-tenured player, as he’s been here since the 2019 season when the Dolphins claimed him from the Baltimore Ravens’ practice squad. Regarding trade rumors, Sieler made it clear his preference was to stay with the Dolphins. Sieler said , “I know people say rumors or talk whatever this time of year, but I’m here focused playing games here, win as a Dolphin, man. And we’re doing a great thing. For Miami, it makes sense to move on, but what’s the right price point? Since 2023, Sieler has 27.5 sacks.” Verderame named the playoff-contending Detroit Lions as a possible trade destination for Sieler. I’m excited for this next week coming up and coming off the bye ready to roll. I love it here. I’ve been here for how long? I want to win here as a Dolphin. I think Hafley, Sully have done an amazing job here. I’m excited to see this team growing and where we’re going and get some wins.” Potential Zach Sieler Trade While Sieler’s preference is to stay in Miami, Dolphins on SI’s Tyler Carmona argued that Miami should at least entertain the idea, as he wrote: “For teams with legitimate postseason aspirations, giving up a draft pick or a promising young player for a proven veteran who could help them win right now might be worth the sacrifice. And in Miami’s case, things can’t get much worse without Sieler, and he won’t be getting any younger by the time the Dolphins are ready to possibly compete again. There’s no question the Ferris State product still has something left in the tank, but another 10-sack season is becoming increasingly difficult to envision. After cranking out double digits in consecutive seasons from 2023 to 2024, his production dipped to 5.5 sacks last year, and he’s at two through five games in 2026… As a team captain, he has value to Miami beyond his play on the field, but the team still would have to at least consider the idea of getting a solid draft pick if given the opportunity.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Dolphins Trade Pitch Sends Key Starter to Super Bowl Contender appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: How to follow US Grand Prix on the BBC
item.description: This will be the 14th edition of the US Grand Prix held at the Circuit of the Americas [Getty Images] Round 18 of the 2026 Formula 1 season heads to the Circuit of the Americas for the United States Grand Prix, from 23-25 October. In the previous race in Singapore, it was a dominant weekend for Max Verstappen who qualified on pole and won for both the sprint and main race - his first victories at the Marina Bay Circuit. The Ferraris were consistently on the Dutchman's tail for the majority of the weekend, but a poor strategy call from Lewis Hamilton meant he could only finish sixth. His team-mate Charles Leclerc finished second with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli third. Antonelli has his first opportunity to secure this year's world title in Austin. For that to happen, the Italian must win the race with Mercedes team-mate Russell ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower. The clocks go back in the UK on race day so we will be on BST for the Friday and Saturday sessions but GMT for the race. Lights out for Sunday's 56-lap race will be at 20:00 GMT. Will Lindblad and Lawson be retained by Racing Bulls? F1 Q&A Session start times and BBC coverage Commentary of the race will be available across BBC Radio 5 Live, 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app. You can also ask your smart speaker to "play 5 Live", for example. Make sure to listen to every episode of the Chequered Flag podcast. For the first time this year, the post-race show for every grand prix is available to watch on BBC iPlayer and YouTube. Friday, 23 October First practice: 18:30-19:30 BST - 5 Sports Extra Second practice: 22:00-23:00 BST - 5 Sports Extra Saturday, 24 October Third practice: 18:30-19:30 BST - 5 Sports Extra Qualifying: 22:00-23:00 BST - 5 Sports Extra Sunday, 25 October Race: 20:00 GMT with build-up from 19:30 - 5 Live Max Verstappen converted his pole into a win last time at the Circuit of the Americas with eventual champion Lando Norris finishing second and Charles Leclerc third [Getty Images] What is the Austin weather forecast? The forecast says it will be sunny and warm across the weekend in Austin, with a gentle breeze and highs of 30C on Friday and Saturday. Sunday's race, which starts at 3pm local time, is set to be dry with temperatures reaching 29C. item.title: “Steph Curry Knows He Messed Up Signing That Contract Extension”: NBA Fans Pity Warriors Star After Blowout Loss to Lakers Sums Up Team’s Current State
item.description: Steph Curry against the Lakers in the season-opening loss © Warriors/X Steph Curry and the Golden State Warriors were given a dose of reality on Wednesday night, dropping their season opener 127-105 to the Los Angeles Lakers on the road. The always-competitive matchup between the Warriors and Lakers turned into a one-sided affair, with LA running roughshod over Golden State in a dominant performance. It would not be fair to say things went awry for the Warriors from tipoff, but it certainly didn’t take long to get out of hand, with Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves feasting on Golden State’s defensive miscues all night long. Curry led the Warriors with 23 points on 7-of-15 shooting. He went 2-of-7 from beyond the 3-point line and was perfect from the charity stripe, going 7-of-7. However, it was not enough to keep Golden State in the game. Fans were frustrated after the loss, and Curry’s dejected look on the bench only added to the concerns. Here’s how fans reacted on social media: “Steph Curry knows he messed up signing that contract extension with the Warriors 😭,” one fan posted on X. Despite a quiet offseason in which the front office made roster improvements through the draft and free agency, the Warriors were exposed in Game 1. While it is only one game, Golden State looked a step behind the Lakers and appeared to be outmatched throughout the contest. It’s Only One Game, but It Was a Disaster The Warriors are the oldest team in the NBA and appeared to be a step behind the Lakers the entire contest. Whether surrendering points in the paint or failing to maintain enough possession to generate quality scoring chances, Golden State looked like they were playing in a completely different league than LA. It’s still early in the season, and the Warriors have a few players nursing minor injuries, but they cannot afford to wait until the injured players return to start making a run. After missing the postseason last year, Golden State simply cannot afford to lapse into the flat mindset they showed in their season opener. As the league’s oldest team, they need to tap into their collective experience and ride out the bad nights. It’s a long season, but it gets late fast. The Warriors get a chance to erase the bad feeling from Wednesday’s loss when they return for Friday night’s home opener against the Memphis Grizzlies. item.title: 🚨 CSD initiates action against Tebas over his anti-RMTV comments
item.description: 🚨 CSD initiates action against Tebas over his anti-RMTV comments Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) has submitted a request to the Administrative Tribunal for Sport (TAD) concerning Javier Tebas over his dispute with Real Madrid. The statement Madrid, October 22, 2026.— Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) submitted a reasoned request to the Administrative Tribunal for Sport (TAD) on Thursday over remarks made against Real Madrid by Javier Tebas, president of LaLiga and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF). In a post on the social media platform X on October 16, Javier Tebas compared Real Madrid’s communication methods to the “propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s Minister of Propaganda”. Acting on its own initiative and within its powers, the CSD has asked the TAD, a collegiate body that acts independently, to assess whether that statement shows evidence of a possible breach of Article 76.4.b of Sports Act 10/1990, which classifies “conspicuous and public acts that undermine sporting dignity or decorum” as serious infringements. In its reasoned request, the CSD refers to the TAD’s own doctrine, which, based on Supreme Court case law, holds that sporting dignity and decorum are linked to a framework of civil coexistence in sport, whose viability requires mutual respect among those holding prominent roles in the field. The CSD believes it is essential for sporting institutions to uphold the values that make sport a place of respect, harmonious coexistence and fair play This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Ranking the top five 2026 Buckeyes heading into the bye week
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes cornerback Jay Timmons (25) reacts during the NCAA football game against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas on Sept. 12, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Ohio State has never been short on talent, and the 2026 season has provided another opportunity for Ryan Day to showcase the depth of his roster. From established playmakers to new rising contributors, several players have stood out as the season has progressed. Ranking the team’s top performers isn’t easy, outside of maybe an obvious name at the top. That being said, taking into account impact, potential, consistency and overall importance to the Buckeyes all factor into the conversation. These are the five who have stood out the most in Ohio State’s 6-1 start to the season and heading into the bye week. No. 5: Earl Little Jr. — Safety Earl Little Jr. had impossibly large shoes to fill coming over to Ohio State, replacing one of the program’s best defensive players ever in Caleb Downs. While it would be incredibly unfair to Little Jr. to compare him to Downs or expect him to immediately match that level of play, the Florida State transfer has been about as good as the Buckeyes could have possibly expected. The veteran safety has become an important part of a continually improving secondary, helping the defense handle opposing passing attacks while also providing support closer to the line of scrimmage in an effort to stop the run. Whether dropping back or playing down in the box, the defensive back has excelled. Little Jr. quietly leads the Buckeyes with 38 tackles on the year, and is also tied for third with four pass breakups. It is no surprise to see him dominate in Columbus, coming off a 2025 season in which he led the Seminoles with 76 tackles — 28 more than the next-best player. Little made his presence felt in Ohio State’s 19-15 win over Indiana, recovering a fumble and recording a team-high eight tackles. His performance demonstrated the value of having an experienced defender who can contribute when the Buckeyes match up against marquee opponents, even if he isn’t the flashiest player on the field. With Ohio State relying on its defensive backs to help anchor the defense, Little’s versatility and physical style make him a valuable contributor. He may not receive the same attention as the team’s biggest stars, but his importance so far this season can’t be denied. No. 4: Carson Hinzman — Center Offensive linemen rarely receive the recognition that skill players enjoy, but Carson Hinzman’s importance to Ohio State’s offense shouldn’t be overlooked. Entering his fourth year as a starter, Hinzman brings valuable experience, communication, and stability to the offensive line. As the starting center, he has responsibilities that extend beyond just winning his individual blocks. That being said, taking into account impact, potential, consistency and overall importance to the Buckeyes all factor into the conversation. These are the five who have stood out the most in Ohio State’s 6-1 start to the season and heading into the bye week. No. 5: Earl Little Jr. — Safety Earl Little Jr. had impossibly large shoes to fill coming over to Ohio State, replacing one of the program’s best defensive players ever in Caleb Downs. While it would be incredibly unfair to Little Jr. to compare him to Downs or expect him to immediately match that level of play, the Florida State transfer has been about as good as the Buckeyes could have possibly expected. The veteran safety has become an important part of a continually improving secondary, helping the defense handle opposing passing attacks while also providing support closer to the line of scrimmage in an effort to stop the run. Whether dropping back or playing down in the box, the defensive back has excelled. Little Jr. quietly leads the Buckeyes with 38 tackles on the year, and is also tied for third with four pass breakups. It is no surprise to see him dominate in Columbus, coming off a 2025 season in which he led the Seminoles with 76 tackles — 28 more than the next-best player. Little made his presence felt in Ohio State’s 19-15 win over Indiana, recovering a fumble and recording a team-high eight tackles. His performance demonstrated the value of having an experienced defender who can contribute when the Buckeyes match up against marquee opponents, even if he isn’t the flashiest player on the field. With Ohio State relying on its defensive backs to help anchor the defense, Little’s versatility and physical style make him a valuable contributor. He may not receive the same attention as the team’s biggest stars, but his importance so far this season can’t be denied. No. 4: Carson Hinzman — Center Offensive linemen rarely receive the recognition that skill players enjoy, but Carson Hinzman’s importance to Ohio State’s offense shouldn’t be overlooked. Entering his fourth year as a starter, Hinzman brings valuable experience, communication, and stability to the offensive line. As the starting center, he has responsibilities that extend beyond just winning his individual blocks. Hinzman helps coordinate the offensive front, recognize defensive looks, and keeps the running and passing games operating smoothly — something that will be even more important now with Julian Sayin out. As one of the elder statesmen up front, his leadership of a unit that has been up-and-down so far this season will be critical as Ohio State enters this tough home stretch of the schedule. It has been a long and winding road for Hinzman to this point. The lineman struggled mightily in his first season with the Buckeyes, and was benched in the 2023 Cotton Bowl after a controversial podcast appearance. Clearly in the dog house, it would have been easy for Hinzman to take the easy way out and hit the transfer portal. Instead, the Wisconsin native stuck it out, and was rewarded with a national title in 2024, of which his offensive line unit was a key driving factor. Hinzman has improved year over year, and is now having his best season to date as the Buckeyes look to again raise the College Football Playoff trophy in the final year of the 12-team bracket just as they did in its inception. His impact is not always obvious in the box score, but dependable offensive line play is essential to a successful offense. Ohio State is still lacking in that department overall, but Hinzman has not been the culprit. No. 3: Jaylen McClain — Safety Jaylen McClain has emerged as one of Ohio State’s most impactful defensive players. Playing free safety, McClain has the responsibility of providing coverage over the top, limiting explosive plays and helping organize the defense from the back end. His production has backed up his importance. McClain recorded eight tackles and four pass breakups earlier this season against Illinois. He also delivered eight tackles against Maryland before adding a sack and a forced fumble in the win over Indiana, which came in a huge spot on fourth down. McClain also nearly intercepted a pass agains the Hoosiers. Overall, McClain leads Ohio State with two interceptions to go along with 32 total tackles, four pass breakups, one tackle for loss and a sack. The New Jersey native is building on his first year as a starter in 2025, where despite being overshadowed by the likes of Downs, Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, McClain showcased his abilities as an excellent last line of defense. McClain’s athleticism and football IQ allows him to contribute both in coverage and as a run defender, making him a particularly valuable piece of the secondary. His performances these last two weeks against Maryland and Indiana have been especially impressive, and Ohio State will need him to continue that hot stretch when they take on a dynamic passing offense at USC in a little over a week. With several big time opponents on the horizon, McClain will have a chance to strengthen his case as one of the Big Ten’s most dependable defensive backs. His consistency and playmaking ability have really stood out in the Ohio State secondary. No. 2: Jay Timmons — Cornerback Speaking of guys standing out in the secondary, Jay Timmons has made a case for himself as one of Ohio State’s best overall players this season — and his career is just getting started. It was a bit shocking at first to see a freshman earn at starting job at cornerback for the Buckeyes, but once games started being played it became immediately clear why he was able to quickly earn that level of trust with the coaching staff. Timmons’ combination of coverage skills, tackling ability and physicality are impressive, and he certainly does not shy away from competition. Timmons’ performance against Indiana was a major highlight of his season. He finished with seven tackles, two pass breakups, and a forced fumble in Ohio State’s narrow victory. It was an especially performance given he was matched up against Charlie Becker, who is likely the No. 2 receiver in college football behind only Jeremiah Smith. What makes Timmons particularly exciting is the level of energy he brings to the secondary. The DB has a sort of presence about him on the field that was sorely missed when he was out for a few weeks with an injury. You saw the immediately impact of his absence in the fourth quarter against Indiana, with the Buckeyes nearly letting up the lead through the air. Timmons’ combination of aggressiveness, playmaking instincts, and early production makes him one of the Buckeyes’ most important players this season. The freshman has already shown that he can deliver in high-pressure situations, and his potential is through the roof. There will be more tests to come, and there is no reason not to trust that Timmons will rise to the occasion. No. 1: Jeremiah Smith — Wide Receiver I’m sure we are all very shocked to see Jeremiah Smith at No. 1 here. He’s the best player at Ohio State, he’s the best player in college football, he’s the best player in the world. The junior wide receiver has continued to establish himself as one of college football’s most dangerous offensive weapons, combining size, speed, body control and an ability to turn routine plays into game-changing moments. Smith’s 2026 camp

item.title: Timberwolves’ LaMelo Ball hilariously shares ‘game plan’ on changing diapers as a dad
item.description: Michael Laughlin-Imagn Images Timberwolves’ LaMelo Ball hilariously shares ‘game plan’ on changing diapers as a dad appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LaMelo Ball has undoubtedly hit the ground running for his new team, the Minnesota Timberwolves . The 25-year-old has formed one of the most potentially entertaining duos in the NBA alongside Anthony Edwards , and will be looking to return to All-Star consideration this campaign. However, there are some jobs Ball himself is not quite cut out to do, and one of them is changing his son, LaOne Ball’s diapers. Speaking to ESPN, LaMelo revealed how it was his partner, Analicia Chaves, who usually changed LaOne’s diapers. “Nah my girl do all that,” he said. “It’s love for sure. We got a good game plan going on, so I know what I gotta do, put bread to the table, she knows what she gotta do, bring to the table…I definitely did it before, it just not my job, you know what I am saying? It’s not my job.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LaMelo on being a dad and whether he changes diapers: "Nah my girl do all that. It's love for sure. I definitely did it before it just not my job" 😂 pic.twitter.com/ZLzP5uzmOh — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 21, 2026 LaOne was born in January 2026, and there is little doubt that changing his diapers probably takes the same amount of skill that LaMelo usually shows on the court. The Timberwolves opened their season with a 131-106 victory over the new-look Miami Heat, with LaMelo’s partner in crime, ANT, starting the campaign in familiar fashion. Edwards scored 45 points and also had 10 rebounds and three assists to show from the game while going 16-29 from shooting, with Ball himself providing some impressive secondary scoring. LaMelo returned with 21 points, six assists and two rebounds from the game, going 7-17 from shooting, and will be well aware that he can improve on that number. For the Heat, Giannis Antetokounmpo top-scored with 35 points and six rebounds, while Bam Adebayo had 15 points and seven rebounds. Miami, as suspected at the start of the season, struggled with their three-point shooting, going converting a paltry eight out of 33 attempts, which meant that they struggled to keep up with an offensively fluid Minnesota team that saw Rudy Gobert grab a whopping 15 rebounds on the night. The Timberwolves will now visit the Orlando Magic for their second game of the season. Related: Timberwolves’ Anthony Edwards tells what he really thinks about LaMelo Ball after Heat win Related: Timberwolves’ Anthony Edwards fires NSFW shot at Heat player who ‘crunk me up’

item.title: Troy Aikman’s 4-Word Position Toward Joe Buck Revealed in Bombshell Report Detailing MNF Argument That ‘Nearly Came to Blows’
item.description: Troy Aikman’s 4-Word Position Toward Joe Buck Revealed in Bombshell Report Detailing MNF Argument That ‘Nearly Came to Blows’ The relationship between Joe Buck and Troy Aikman has reportedly hit a rough patch after their prolonged time working together in the broadcast booth. Ahead of ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast in Los Angeles last week, the duo reportedly got into a heated confrontation. The incident took place before the Buffalo Bills defeated the Los Angeles Rams in overtime. New details have now been revealed about the disagreement, with contract negotiations and ESPN’s plans for the future of its broadcasting team at the center of the controversy. Troy Aikman-Joe Buck Tensions Escalate After Secret Contract Talks According to In Touch , the tension between Buck and Aikman escalated to the point where they nearly “came to blows” during a recent argument. Puck reporter Dylan Byers later provided more details about the situation on Wednesday, citing a source with direct knowledge of the matter. According to Byers, the disagreement stemmed from weeks of growing frustration on Aikman’s part. The source described the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback as becoming “increasingly cold” and difficult to deal with. “Joe finally snapped,” the source told Byers , referring to the Week 5 incident at the Bills-Rams game. “He basically said, ‘Dude, are we really going to do this?’ And Troy’s position was: You (expletive) me over!” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Buck’s six-year ESPN extension became public in September, but Byers reported that the agreement had actually been reached months earlier, in May, without Aikman’s knowledge. According to the report, neither Buck nor ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro informed Aikman about the deal before it became public. Buck’s extension reportedly also included an understanding that he could have a different broadcast partner beginning in 2027. Meanwhile, Aikman is entering the final season of the five-year contract he signed in 2022, with his current deal scheduled to expire after Super Bowl LXI in February 2027. The timing of the negotiations reportedly left Aikman feeling blindsided as he “saw it as the ultimate act of betrayal.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “They cut this deal in May and put it in a drawer,” Byers’ report says. “ESPN didn’t tell him, Joe didn’t tell him.” The uncertainty surrounding Aikman’s future has also fueled speculation about who could join Buck in the MNF booth if ESPN decides to make a change. Reports last week indicated that ESPN had already held discussions with Greg Olsen, whose contract with Fox is set to expire at the end of the current season. Meanwhile, Buck would also reportedly be interested in working with Olsen if he becomes available. However, Buck has attempted to ease tensions and foster a more professional atmosphere within the broadcasting team. According to Byers’ report, Buck apologized to Aikman and

item.title: Ex-NFL Star Urges Eagles To Replace Jalen Hurts With Joe Milton
item.description: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton III. Getty FRISCO, TEXAS - AUGUST 25: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys throws during practice at The Star in Frisco on August 25, 2026 in Frisco, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) Getty Phil Simms believes that former Cowboys quarterback is capable of being a starter in the NFL Getty GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys drops back to pass during the first quarter of the preseason NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty The Philadelphia Eagles could soon have a quarterback controversy. With Jalen Hurts out for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season, Tanner McKee has taken over as the starter. While the Eagles have been confident in McKee in the past, this season has been different. Heading into the start of the 2026 NFL season, the Eagles initially named McKee the third-string quarterback behind Andy Dalton. Getty FRISCO, TEXAS – AUGUST 25: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys throws during practice at The Star in Frisco on August 25, 2026 in Frisco, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) Eventually, Dalton played his way into a demotion before getting cut. McKee might have the keys to the offense, but his leash is going to be short. The Eagles could replace him with the rookie Cole Payton, or they could utilize Joe Milton. The former New England Patriots star Rob Gronkowski would like to see the latter. Ex-NFL Star Urges Eagles To Replace Jalen Hurts With Joe Milton Getty Phil Simms believes that former Cowboys quarterback is capable of being a starter in the NFL “It’s not a thing that we might see Joe Milton. We need to see Joe Milton. There’s been a lot of controversy on why he left New England, a lot of controversy on why he was on the practice squad with Dallas and cut. We need to see him. I was happy to see him picked up with the Philadelphia Eagles once we saw the situation and what we saw with Jalen Hurts going on IR,” Gronkowski said on Up & Adams this week . “With Joe Milton, he needs an opportunity. I think he’s an unbelievable athlete. I think he needs another opportunity to shine. I think he’s going to get it in Philadelphia. He’s fun to watch. I liked watching him when he was here in New England, when he played in the preseason games.” The Eagles carried four quarterbacks for most of the season when they had Jalen Hurts in the lineup. After he went out, they needed another body in the QB room. Milton was sitting on the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. He was considered a surprising cut by the Cowboys after his preseason action. Will The Eagles Replace Tanner McKee? Getty GLENDALE, ARIZONA – AUGUST 22: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys drops back to pass during the first quarter of the preseason NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty

He completed 26 passes for 215 yards. The quarterback connected with DeVonta Smith for his lone touchdown of the day. The Eagles lost 24-15. Since McKee has been around for the past few years, and spent the entire season with the Eagles, he should continue to play. However, if McKee’s struggles continue, the Eagles certainly wouldn’t be wrong to consider trying something new with Milton, who has thrown for just 424 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions throughout his career. item.title: Eagles Film Analysis: Can empty formations help solve the offense’s pressure problems?
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles catches a snap during a game against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images All statistics come from the Fantasy Points Data Suite or from NFL Pro in this one. A bonus article! The Eagles’ protection sucks right now. Four-weak pressures and other pressure packages are a major part of today’s NFL, and the Eagles desperately need better answers. They cannot keep allowing pressure to destroy the entire operation before the quarterback has a chance to do anything. Whether it’s Jalen Hurts or Tanner McKee, give the quarterback and the players around him a chance to execute. I’ve posted a full video on Patreon breaking down these issues, combining the numbers with film examples to explain what’s going wrong and what the Eagles could do about it. I’d appreciate you checking it out if you want to learn more about how I use stats and film together, or simply join me in getting increasingly annoyed at how incompetent this offense looks right now. Here’s a little spoiler… Special video for Patreon! A behind-the-scenes look at how I combine data/film, breaking down the Eagles' pass protection struggles and how they can improve. This stuff should not be difficult for the offensive staff to see. Here's a little clip of the moment I realized just how… pic.twitter.com/DxIzVYHw9D — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 21, 2026 This post shows how straightforward basic self-scouting can be. You don’t need to uncover some revolutionary concept. Look at what happens under pressure, identify where you’ve succeeded, and watch the film to understand why. Then work out whether those successful ideas can become a bigger part of the offense. The numbers should prompt questions, and the film should help answer them. One obvious place to start is formation. Spread the defense out, make the potential threats easier to identify and give the quarterback clear answers to establish some rhythm. Empty won’t magically fix every protection issue, but there is enough encouraging evidence here to warrant using it more. This stuff shouldn’t be this hard. I’m bored of hearing about the Eagles’ pass protection woes, so I thought I’d look at how formation can help them for the rest of the year. This isn’t a normal film breakdown for me, but I wanted to look at some statistics and what is going on. As often, this post was inspired by this graph from the wonderful Deniz Selman. #Eagles are still the only team in the NFL to have zero successful under center play action plays when blitzed. They have an 0/18 (0%) success rate & are losing an average of almost a full expected point when they run UC PA and get blitzed. pic.twitter.com/T1WpcmlUUK — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 21, 2026 That is one of the most insane graphs I’ve ever seen after 6 weeks of a season. It’s not Week 2 anymore! Anyway,

(Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images All statistics come from the Fantasy Points Data Suite or from NFL Pro in this one. A bonus article! The Eagles’ protection sucks right now. Four-weak pressures and other pressure packages are a major part of today’s NFL, and the Eagles desperately need better answers. This stuff should not be difficult for the offensive staff to see. Here's a little clip of the moment I realized just how… pic.twitter.com/DxIzVYHw9D — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 21, 2026 This post shows how straightforward basic self-scouting can be. You don’t need to uncover some revolutionary concept. Look at what happens under pressure, identify where you’ve succeeded, and watch the film to understand why. Then work out whether those successful ideas can become a bigger part of the offense. The numbers should prompt questions, and the film should help answer them. One obvious place to start is formation. Spread the defense out, make the potential threats easier to identify and give the quarterback clear answers to establish some rhythm. Empty won’t magically fix every protection issue, but there is enough encouraging evidence here to warrant using it more. This stuff shouldn’t be this hard. I’m bored of hearing about the Eagles’ pass protection woes, so I thought I’d look at how formation can help them for the rest of the year. This isn’t a normal film breakdown for me, but I wanted to look at some statistics and what is going on. As often, this post was inspired by this graph from the wonderful Deniz Selman. #Eagles are still the only team in the NFL to have zero successful under center play action plays when blitzed. They have an 0/18 (0%) success rate & are losing an average of almost a full expected point when they run UC PA and get blitzed. pic.twitter.com/T1WpcmlUUK — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 21, 2026 That is one of the most insane graphs I’ve ever seen after 6 weeks of a season. It’s not Week 2 anymore! Anyway, let’s look at some results and what the Eagles can do differently. What the data shows Let’s start with the Eagles’ overall results under pressure. Empty has been their most productive formation, while under center (singleback) has been a complete disaster. There are only 12 pressured plays from empty, so nobody should pretend this proves it will solve everything. However, when your offense keeps falling apart under pressure, surely you should explore the situations where it has actually functioned? Next, look at the target depth under pressure. The intermediate production stands out. Beating pressure doesn’t have to mean throwing behind the line of scrimmage or launching a desperate deep shot. Opportunities exist to attack the space behind the rush, but route combinations, timing, and protection rules must give the quarterback access to those throws. “Get the ball out” means very little without somewhere useful to throw it. There is no surprise that throwing deep or behind the LOS hasn’t worked. The stats match the eye test. 2) The Eagles had a couple of nice plays from under center in this game, which we will get to later, but this was another failure. They still don't have an answer for the CB blitz. They can't successfully get Hurts on the move because they can't stop unblocked defenders appearing… pic.twitter.com/FwqRGboXzw — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Now let’s narrow it to five-plus rushers generating pressure within 2.5 seconds. Empty still stands out. It’s only four plays, but these are precisely the situations that have been destroying this offense. When pressure arrives that quickly, the answer needs to be built into the play. You cannot expect either quarterback to repeatedly escape and rescue a concept that hasn’t had time to develop. Surely, the staff is looking at this? Here’s empty against five-plus rushers overall. Spreading the defense out can help the quarterback assess the coverage and potential rush before the snap. It also gives him five receiving options, with opportunities to replace blitzing defenders. That still requires coherent protection and hot routes, particularly when six come against five blockers, but at least it gives the quarterback a lot of information pre-snap. It’s easier when you know only six can blitz. No one is blitzing empty with 7 defenders, so you only have to work out who the +1 rusher can be. 4) Hey, we did see the Eagles have a plan for some pressure in this game! That's a start! They went to Empty formations a lot to make it easier for Hurts and the offense, and it worked! Hurts gets the CB to show his hand pre-snap, then throws it right to Wicks, who turns around… pic.twitter.com/XCd35BNqsa — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 The wider shotgun sample shows that simply putting the quarterback in the gun isn’t enough. Spacing, route distribution, and the number of available receivers matter too. I want an offense that helps McKee to identify the problem and deliver the ball with confidence. Empty is one way to simplify that picture and establish some rhythm. Then there’s under-center against five-plus rushers. Come on. Fifteen plays without a single successful one is horrendous. Turning your back to the defense on play-action makes it harder to identify and respond to pressure, especially when the protection keeps breaking down. How long do you keep asking players to execute something that produces absolutely nothing? Finally, this gets even more interesting when you look at the number of route runners against five-plus rushers. With three or fewer, the Eagles average 0.6 yards per play. With four, that rises to 3.5. With five, it jumps to 6.3, alongside positive EPA. These are different play samples, so context matters, but keeping extra players in protection clearly hasn’t guaranteed better results. Sending five out gives the defense more receiving threats to account for and the quarterback more answers. That deserves serious attention. The Eagles’ tight ends and running backs are not good in pass protection. How about we stop asking them to do it? Final Thoughts Empty won’t magically fix the Eagles’ protection, but the numbers give them an obvious place to start. Spread things out, build in clear answers, and give McKee and the rest of the offense a chance to find some rhythm. The stats do not lie. The frustrating part is how straightforward this is to identify through basic self-scouting. If you watch the video on Patreon, all of this takes less than 20 minutes to work out. It’s not difficult. The coaching staff has far more information than we do, yet the same problems keep destroying the offense. At some point, they have to adapt to what is actually happening on the field. Obviously, better players will help improve pass protection, but the Eagles’ coaches have to consider their formation to prevent problems from occurring. Thank you for reading! I’d love to hear your thoughts, so feel free to comment below

item.title: 4 Bold Predictions for Minnesota Vikings vs Indianapolis Colts
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL analysts may not be giving the Minnesota Vikings a ton of credit for their 5-0 start. But as one of just three remaining undefeated teams, this group has to be feeling confident heading into Week 7 following their bye. Next up is a 2-4 Indianapolis Colts team that just fired their longtime general manager after losing their second consecutive game. After showing some tangible growth on offense, Vikings fans are eager to watch the next game on Sunday. Are the Vikings facing a trap game? Or will they capitalize on facing a Colts team that is suddenly looking lost? It’s time to dive into four bold predictions for Sunday’s Colts-Vikings game . Related: 5 Jonathan Taylor Trade Destinations That Make Sense Before NFL Deadline Kyler Murray’s 300-Yard Game Inspires Fanbase Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) drops back to pass against New Orleans Saints during the first half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The start of Kyler Murray’s tenure with the Vikings has been a bit of a rollercoaster. From tossing an interception on his first attempt to being ruled out of his season debut in the first quarter, Murray’s early experience in Minnesota couldn’t have gone worse. Yet, the former No. 1 overall pick’s luck has turned in the past two outings, completing 76.1% of his passes, averaging 271 yards per game (counting his rushing). That’s a formula the Vikings can win with, yet this time, Murray will have his first combined 300-yard game with his new team, and suddenly Kevin O’Connell’s group will start to get a lot more respect. Related: 1 NFL Player From Each Team Who Will Disappoint in Week 7, Including Sam Darnold Vikings Defense Forces Four Turnovers Jan 13, 2025; Glendale, AZ, USA; Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores against the Los Angeles Rams during an NFC wild card game at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Last year, Vikings fans were upset because Sam Darnold and Daniel Jones were playing like MVP candidates. Eventually, Jones started to stumble as he suffered injuries, including a torn Achilles, and we all know where Darnold ended up. Both QBs are now struggling, but Jones in particular may even be on the verge of being benched. Jones has already committed nine turnovers, and Jonathan Taylor has lost two fumbles. Look for those trends to continue on Sunday against the NFL’s best defense. Related: 5 Minnesota Vikings Trades To Capitalize on 5-0 Start Harrison Smith Records First INT of Season Jan 4, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell greets Minnesota Vikings safety Harrison Smith (22) against the Green Bay Packers during the fourth quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Harrison Smith has returned for one more year, but he hasn’t had a profound impact on the defense, at least from a production standp

item.title: Benefits of extending Adrian Morejon qualifying offer
item.description: San Diego Padres reliever Adrian Morejon (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Offseason media speculation has suggested the San Diego Padres are leaning toward extending Adrian Morejon a qualifying offer. The lefty pitcher earned consideration with a dominant second half. No question, Morejon should be brought back for the 2027 campaign. It is rare for a setup reliever to receive a qualifying offer, but this news should not come as a big surprise. Morejon is considered the top left-handed reliever in this winter’s free-agent class, and should command plenty of interest on the open market. What is a qualifying offer? Every organization has five days after the World Series ends to extend a qualifying offer to an impending free agent. It is a one-year contract offer, and this year’s price tag is $23.15 million. However, all players must have spent the entire season on the club’s roster and have never received a qualifying offer in their career. If they decline the contract offer and sign elsewhere, their former team receives a compensatory draft pick. Why extend a qualifying offer Re-signing Morejon should be the Padres’ top priority this offseason. The club has no internal left-handed bullpen option to replace him. In fact, it is hard to find a reliever who can take on his workload: he averaged over 70 appearances over the last three seasons. View Link In 2025, Morejon posted a 2.83 ERA over 86.0 innings pitched. Pairing an outstanding 30.4% strikeout rate with a solid 8.0% walk rate, Morejon struck out 107 batters. Perhaps his most impressive underlying metric, Morejon surrendered just four home runs last season. If he rejects the offer, his suitors will have to consider the cost of pursuing him. Fortunately for the Friars, they receive compensation if their premier setup reliever signs with another team. If accepted, Morejon would receive a massive salary increase from his $3.9 million mark a year ago. San Diego keeps its late-inning bullpen tandem for another season. Extending the qualifying offer puts the ball in Morejon’s court. Morejon has a life-changing decision At 27, Morejon is in the prime of his career. Most free agents would decline the qualifying offer to seek a multi-year, big-money deal. Morejon’s potential suitors do not need a reminder of his value to the bullpen. Still, a conflicted decision looms. While accepting the qualifying offer is a foolish business decision, Morejon has openly expressed a desire to remain in San Diego. A deep-seated loyalty to the franchise could play a role in his decision. To extend a qualifying offer, the Padres have to be confident Morejon is open to a long-term extension. It would not be a surprise to see the Padres and Morejon come together on a new deal. Time will tell what occurs. In this edition of his player report card, Lincoln Zdunich of Gaslamp Ball looks at starter/reliever Jhony Brito . Baseball News: The Tampa Bay Rays stumbled upon a key piece of their roster who has helped them reach the World Series. Pat Murphy led the Milwaukee Brewers to the best record in baseball. Can he lead them to a World Series title ? Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani will not need surgery to fix what ails him. Tarik Skubal will be the prized free agent on the market this offseason. Where he lands is anyone’s guess. Brian Cashman will return as the general manager for the New York Yankees. Kurt Suzuki will not return for a second season as manager of the Los Angeles Angels.

item.title: Texas vs Ole Miss football predictions: Betting lines, TV channel/streaming for Week 8
item.description: Texas Longhorns running back Raleek Brown (0) runs the ball in the fourth quarter of Texas' 20-17 win over Tennessee at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee, Sept. 26, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football has dropped two straight games in the same season for the first time since 2021 while tumbling from its spot atop the polls. Things don't get any easier for the No. 19 Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) Saturday at Royal-Memorial Stadium against visiting Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1). The No. 7 Rebels boast a Heisman Trophy candidate in quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , and they've beaten three ranked teams behind a dynamic offense and a rock-solid defense. Texas has to face three ranked teams in its final six games of the regular season as well as two old rivals in Arkansas and Texas A&M. If the Longhorns want to remain in contention for a spot in the College Football Playoff, they'll have to beat Ole Miss . Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Ole Miss Rebels. No. 19 Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) vs. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) When: 6:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: The weather won't be as crisp as last week, but temperatures will still be in the low 80s at kickoff and dip into the 60s by the fourth quarter. Clear skies, full hearts for football fans. MORE: Fans turning on you is one thing, but former Texas players, too? That's a problem | Golden Texas vs Ole Miss football betting info Moneyline: Texas -165 / Ole Miss +135 Spread: Texas is favored by 3 points. Over/under : 53½ Texas history: Ole Miss All-time: Texas leads 6-2 Last meeting: Ole Miss 44, Texas 23 (Sept. 14, 2013) Most memorable meeting: Texas 12, Ole Miss 7 (1962). In a top-5 meeting that capped the 1961 regular season, the Longhorns held on for a hard-fought 12-7 win in the Cotton Bowl. The favored Rebels outgained Texas in yardage, 319-183, but the Longhorns had three interceptions, including three by Jerry Cook. For fifth-year coach Darrell Royal, the victory gave him his first 10-win season at Texas as well as his first bowl triumph. Royal would go on to six more 10-win seasons and seven more bowl wins at Texas before retiring after the 1976 season. MORE: Steve Sarkisian evaluated 'everything' after Texas football loss. item.content:encoded: Texas Longhorns running back Raleek Brown (0) runs the ball in the fourth quarter of Texas' 20-17 win over Tennessee at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee, Sept. 26, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football has dropped two straight games in the same season for the first time since 2021 while tumbling from its spot atop the polls.
