No. 19 Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) vs. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) When: 6:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: The weather won't be as crisp as last week, but temperatures will still be in the low 80s at kickoff and dip into the 60s by the fourth quarter. Clear skies, full hearts for football fans. MORE: Fans turning on you is one thing, but former Texas players, too? That's a problem | Golden Texas vs Ole Miss football betting info Moneyline: Texas -165 / Ole Miss +135 Spread: Texas is favored by 3 points. Over/under : 53½ Texas history: Ole Miss All-time: Texas leads 6-2 Last meeting: Ole Miss 44, Texas 23 (Sept. 14, 2013) Most memorable meeting: Texas 12, Ole Miss 7 (1962). In a top-5 meeting that capped the 1961 regular season, the Longhorns held on for a hard-fought 12-7 win in the Cotton Bowl. The favored Rebels outgained Texas in yardage, 319-183, but the Longhorns had three interceptions, including three by Jerry Cook. For fifth-year coach Darrell Royal, the victory gave him his first 10-win season at Texas as well as his first bowl triumph. Royal would go on to six more 10-win seasons and seven more bowl wins at Texas before retiring after the 1976 season. MORE: Steve Sarkisian evaluated 'everything' after Texas football loss. Are changes coming? Know the foe: Ole Miss Last week: Beat Missouri, 31-3 Players to watch: QB Trinidad Chambliss , a 6-foot-1, 205-pound senior, won a court battle with the NCAA in the offseason for a sixth year of eligibility. He's beating plenty of defenses, too; he ranks second in the SEC with 279.3 yards passing per game and has accounted for 20 total touchdowns. RB Kewan Lacey , a 5-11, 205-pound junior from the Dallas suburb of Lancaster, earned all-SEC accolades last season but has battled injuries while carrying the ball 62 times for 352 yards and five touchdowns this season. But he looked plenty healthy last week with a season-high 122 yards against Missouri. LB Suntarine Perkins, a 6-2, 220-pound senior, is off to a quiet start with just 20 tackles and 1½ sacks. But he has 21 sacks in his career, and he's the twitchy kind of edge rusher that has given the Texas line fits this season. Central Texas connections: Freshman quarterback Reese Wise hasn't played this season but boasts some pedigree considering he comes from the quarterback factory at Westlake High School.… Former blue-chip receiver recruit Johntay Cook II signed with Texas in 2023 and appeared in 20 games over two seasons for the Longhorns before transferring to Syracuse. Now in his first season at Ole Miss, he has just one catch for -3 yards. When Texas has the ball Could Raleek Brown be the workhorse this week? He looks like the only healthy back since freshman Derrek Cooper missed last week's game with an undisclosed injury and Hollywood Smothers missed practice earlier in the week with a reported arm or shoulder injury. Brown did rip off a 32-yard run against Florida but had just 15 yards on seven other carries. Ole Miss held Missouri to 39 yards on 26 carries behind a dominant effort from DT Will Echoles, and the Texas offensive line has struggled in short-yardage situations against Oklahoma and Florida. Quarterback Arch Manning talks about "letting it rip," but the fourth-year quarterback has struggled this season while averaging only 215.8 yards a game on 63.9% passing. Ole Miss ranks just 11 th in the SEC in pass defense with 233.3 yards allowed per game, and Missouri's Donovan Olugbode exploded for nine catches and 128 yards. High-paid Auburn transfer Cam Coleman (20 catches, 336 yards, 6 TDs) will try and do the same. MORE: Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning fight for blame in Texas football's offensive struggles When Ole Miss has the ball Texas may have to play without All-American edge rusher Colin Simmons , who leads the nation with 10 ½ sacks but will likely miss the game with a reported ankle injury. Tackle Maraad Waston (three sacks) is the only other Longhorn with more than one sack, which is bad news against an Ole Miss offensive line that has allowed an SEC-low five sacks all season. The Rebels only trail Georgia when it comes to yards per carry in the SEC with an impressive 5.15 in league play, but they've also run it just a league-low 190 times in all games. Texas allows a league-low 103.7 yards rushing a game in SEC play, which means Chambliss could air it out more than usual to a receiving corps led by Deuce Alexander (19 catches, 275 yards). Texas running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs the ball during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Ole Miss key matchup Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles vs. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. With Simmons likely out for the game, Rasheem Biles needs to step up as a playmaker after going three straight games without a takeaway or a forced fumble. And he'll have to do it while keeping an eye on the slippery Chambliss, who has rushed for 127 yards this season. Texas vs Ole Miss prediction Thomas Jones: Ole Miss 28, Texas 24. The Longhorns' offense has its best game in league play, but the expected absence of Simmons is too much to overcome against arguably the top quarterback in the nation. Danny Davis: Texas. I feel like this is a version of the Anakin Skywalker meme where Padmé asks "There is no way that the Longhorns' football season essentially ends before Halloween, right?," gets a blank stare from Anakin and then has to desperately state the question again. Texas wins this game for no other reason than it has to. Michael Shapiro: Ole Miss 28, Texas 27 . This is a perfect emotional spot for the Longhorns, who will take the field with plenty of fire with their backs against the wall. I still can't shake the matchup concerns. Ole Miss has perhaps the best quarterback in college football in Trinidad Chambliss. Texas will be without edge rusher Colin Simmons, perhaps college football's best defensive player. Add in the defensive chops of Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding, and a bounce-back for Texas is no guarantee. Expect a close, dramatic contest Saturday night, one that will ultimately end in another Longhorns disappointment. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. This article originally published at Texas vs Ole Miss football predictions: Betting lines, TV channel/streaming for Week 8 .

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly faces suspension and a $285 fine after Portugal walkout
item.description: Source: Dziurek/Depositphotos vverve/Depositphotos Cristiano Ronaldo receives Portugal ban Cristiano Ronaldo received a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine, approximately $285, from the Portuguese Football Federation on October 19, 2026. The punishment followed his unauthorized departure from Portugal’s national team camp. The 41-year-old Al Nassr forward left the squad in Copenhagen, Denmark, on September 30 after a disagreement with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus. The team was preparing for a UEFA Nations League match against Denmark. natursports/Depositphotos Cristiano Ronaldo leaves Copenhagen camp Cristiano Ronaldo departed Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen on September 30, 2026, before a scheduled training session. Euronews reported that the session was planned at Parken Stadium ahead of Portugal’s upcoming match against Denmark. The Portuguese Football Federation’s disciplinary findings stated that Ronaldo left without informing federation officials or teammates beforehand. The ruling also described a subsequent telephone conversation between Ronaldo and the federation President, Pedro Proença, regarding his departure. jenta/Depositphotos Cristiano Ronaldo disputes his playing role Cristiano Ronaldo’s disagreement with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus concerned his expected playing time during the September and October 2026 UEFA Nations League fixtures. Ronaldo accused the coach of breaking promises about his role on 2 occasions. Jesus denied reaching an agreement with Ronaldo about playing time. Reuters reported that the coach nevertheless left open the possibility of Ronaldo returning to Portugal’s squad once the disagreement had been addressed. m.iacobucci.tiscali.it/Depositphotos Cristiano Ronaldo stays on Norway bench Cristiano Ronaldo remained an unused substitute during Portugal’s September 27, 2026, UEFA Nations League victory over Norway. The forward did not enter the match despite being available for selection during the international fixture. AFP reported that Ronaldo subsequently learned he would not start against Denmark on October 1. The selection disagreement contributed to tensions with coach Jorge Jesus before the forward left Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen. olegda88.gmail.com/Depositphotos Cristiano Ronaldo faces disciplinary case Cristiano Ronaldo faced disciplinary proceedings under Article 160 of the Portuguese Football Federation’s regulations. Reuters reported that the investigation opened on October 9, 2026, after the federation was alerted to the events 2 days earlier. The federation’s disciplinary council concluded that Ronaldo had deliberately left the national team without authorization. Its October 19 decision established responsibility for the violation and imposed sanctions under the applicable disciplinary rules. m.iacobucci.tiscali.it/Depositphotos Cristiano Ronaldo receives reduced penalty Cristiano Ronaldo received a 30-day suspension after the Portuguese Football Federation considered mitigating circums

item.title: 3 Titans players who could help replace DT Jordan Elliott
item.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Solomon Thomas #90 of the Tennessee Titans looks on during the second half of the Week 3 preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans released veteran defensive tackle Jordan Elliott earlier this week . The complete details are now available. A to Z Sports and Easton Freeze reported Elliott allegedly threatened a teammate ( reportedly JC Latham ) with gun violence, even showing intent before the situation was calmed. Unacceptable stuff. Naturally, the Titans released Elliott even though head coach Robert Saleh vouched for him to receive a future opportunity elsewhere during Wednesday’s presser. Elliott was playing quality football as a rotational defensive lineman after signing a two-year contract with the team in free agency. Saleh, Aaron Whitecotton, and Mike Borgonzi must deal with the fallout. We’ve identified three Titans players who could help the defensive line replace Elliott. Nazir Stackhouse Nose tackle Nazir Stackhouse helped replace Elliott in Sunday’s Week 6 win over the Colts. He served as the primary interior run stopper behind Jeffery Simmons and John Franklin-Myers. Remember, that is essentially the role Elliott was playing. The Titans claimed Stackhouse off waivers from the Green Bay Packers after final cuts. He played well as a big-bodied space eater. Solomon Thomas The Titans brought Elliott to Tennessee as a free agent this past offseason partially because he played for Coach Saleh before. Understanding his system is vital to the success of the scheme. Well, following Elliott’s departure, the only Titans interior defender on the roster who has played for Saleh before is veteran DT Solomon Thomas. Timmy Horne When the Titans ruled out Elliott for Sunday’s game versus the Colts, they made Timmy Horne a gameday call-up. The four-year pro ended up playing a sizable 25 snaps. Horne is listed as being 312 pounds via the team’s official website; he’s a more traditional nose tackle who can play a similar role to Elliott. With the Titans having an open spot on the 53-man roster following Elliott’s release, promoting Horne from the practice squad would make sense.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan’s former star WR believes he’ll never win a Super Bowl
item.description: SEATTLE, WA - OCTOBER 11: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers awards a game ball to Mike Evans #5 in the locker room after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. The 49ers defeated the Seahawks 32-29. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are at the top of the NFL right now, sitting at 6-0 after their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders. After starting the year with the third-best odds in their own division, the 49ers are the clear frontrunners to win the NFC and currently stand as the favorites to win the Super Bowl at +600, according to FanDuel. San Francisco has been clicking everywhere this season, despite their bevy of injuries. Behind MVP-level play from Brock Purdy and an elite No. 1 receiver in Mike Evans, the 49ers offense has been quite efficient throughout the year. The defense, on the other hand, has overcome the loss of Nick Bosa over the last few weeks to be a strong finishing team with a ton of growing young talent under Raheem Morris. Even with the injuries, it feels like this could be the year for the 49ers, and they’ll get a chance to get a lot of players healthy following their bye in Week 8. Ultimately, it will come down to the playoffs, where the 49ers have had their moments over the last seven years, but have come up short in their pursuit of the Super Bowl. They made it there in 2019, lost in the NFC Championship Game in 2021 and 2022, made it there again in 2023, and then lost in the divisional round last year. Will Kyle Shanahan finally get his Super Bowl here in 2026? That team starts very fast every year. The only time they haven’t started fast is when they had everybody hurt. And this year they’re still managing to get people hurt, but they’re off to a good start. I think, me personally, that he’s a great offensive mind, right? “But in tough situations, in pressure situations, the over-aggressive play calls always get him in trouble. And I think that’s just his mentality. He doesn’t play situational football well. That’s the only thing that I think that’s really like a knock on his game. And the thing that he does, he doesn’t play like situational football well. And that gets his team in trouble when you play against great quarterbacks. item.content:encoded: SEATTLE, WA - OCTOBER 11: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers awards a game ball to Mike Evans #5 in the locker room after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. The 49ers defeated the Seahawks 32-29. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are at the top of the NFL right now, sitting at 6-0 after their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders. After starting the year with the third-best odds in their own division, the 49ers are the clear frontrunners to win the NFC and currently stand as the favorites to win the Super Bowl at +600, according to FanDuel. San Francisco has been clicking everywhere this season, despite their bevy of injuries. Behind MVP-level play from Brock Purdy and an elite No. 1 receiver in Mike Evans, the 49ers offense has been quite efficient throughout the year. The defense, on the other hand, has overcome the loss of Nick Bosa over the last few weeks to be a strong finishing team with a ton of growing young talent under Raheem Morris. Even with the injuries, it feels like this could be the year for the 49ers, and they’ll get a chance to get a lot of players healthy following their bye in Week 8. Ultimately, it will come down to the playoffs, where the 49ers have had their moments over the last seven years, but have come up short in their pursuit of the Super Bowl. They made it there in 2019, lost in the NFC Championship Game in 2021 and 2022, made it there again in 2023, and then lost in the divisional round last year. Will Kyle Shanahan finally get his Super Bowl here in 2026? One of his former star receivers, Roddy White, doesn’t believe so, and also doesn’t ever see him winning a ring for a few reasons. “No,” White said when asked about Shanahan winning a ring during his career on The Up And Adams Show. “They start like this every year. That team starts very fast every year. The only time they haven’t started fast is when they had everybody hurt. And this year they’re still managing to get people hurt, but they’re off to a good start. I think, me personally, that he’s a great offensive mind, right? “But in tough situations, in pressure situations, the over-aggressive play calls always get him in trouble. And I think that’s just his mentality. He doesn’t play situational football well. That’s the only thing that I think that’s really like a knock on his game. And the thing that he does, he doesn’t play like situational football well. And that gets his team in trouble when you play against great quarterbacks. And when you make it to a Super Bowl, you’re gonna be playing against a great quarterback.” The four-time Pro Bowl receiver for the Atlanta Falcons believes Shanahan has yet to learn game management and handling those situations in playoff games. “Your ability to understand the flow of the game and the things like that is going to help you win those games,” White continued. “And I think especially if you have to play Patrick Mahomes in the Super Bowl. That guy has learned from Tom Brady, just playing him each and every year, playing him in Super Bowls. He knows what it takes. He can read what’s going on. He knows how to handle those situations, and he always comes out as a winner because he doesn’t give himself an opportunity to lose the game. And I think that Kyle always thinks about I have to win the game. I have to win the game instead of putting his players in the best position to win the game. “He’s a great play caller, like great play caller. The play call sheet is deep. I will say that. But he seems to have a guy that can handle it. Being a part of that and just doing everything when Matt [Ryan] was there and going through everything. I mean, man, we’ll be on the sideline, and he’ll see something, boom, boom, boom. He’d be like, hey, man, I know we didn’t work this in practice, but it’s gonna work. Hey, this is what I want you to do. Boom, go out there, extra eye, execute the play, works. Boom, explosive play. So he’s very, very smart. I just think the aggressive play calling when not needed in pressure situations always gets the best of him.” Shanahan’s game management, especially in go-for situations, had been one of the more scrutinized parts of him as a head coach earlier in his career. He had generally been too conservative in those situations and often went against analytics with his decisions. That has changed over the past few years, but White believes he’s gotten too aggressive as a play-caller. So far this season, he’s been having a great year after arguably the best coaching season of his career in 2025 with a battered 49ers team. We’ll see if that can translate to postseason success, but the 49ers are putting themselves in a great spot to be successful in January with their start to the season.

item.title: Predicting upsets in Week 7 of NFL season
item.description: Last week in the NFL we were right about two upsets and just missed a third one by 3 points. This week, we have identified new teams poised to pull off an unexpected victory. Let’s jump right in and see which teams can pull off a shocking win in Week 7. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 7 of 2026 NFL season New Orleans Saints over the Pittsburgh Steelers Sep 27, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough (6) throws in the fourth quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The Steelers travel to France at 4-2, tied for the AFC North lead after defeating the Bucs in Tampa last weekend. The Saints righted the ship after three straight losses with an impressive 34-27 win over the Giants. For the purposes of scheduling, the Saints are the home team this Sunday, and it seems fitting as New Orleans is the “Frenchest” city in America. This doesn’t necessarily mean the Saints will enjoy any “home field edge,” since the Steelers traditionally travel very well. We’re picking the Saints here mainly because today’s NFL is a league where teams aren’t quite as good as they look when they win, and aren’t quite as bad as they look in their losses. These two teams are pretty evenly matched on both sides of the ball, and it wouldn’t be much of a surprise to see Aaron Rodgers have one of his “Bad Aaron” days. The Steelers feel more like a 4-3 team than a 5-2 team, and the Saints at 3-4 would still be very much in the mix in the NFC South. The bottom line: the Saints need this game more than the Steelers do right now, so we’re picking them to win this game in France. Final Score: Saints 24 – Steelers 23 Tennessee Titans over the Cleveland Browns Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (98) causes and recovers a fumble Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, by Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Both teams are coming off of victories as the Browns travel to Music City to take on the previously winless Titans. While the Titans likely didn’t figure everything out last week in their win over the Colts, it was certainly a step in the right direction. The Browns managed to eke out a 13-10 triumph in a snoozer against the Lamar-less Ravens. While the Titans aren’t an offensive juggernaut, they can do a little better than that. Jeffery Simmons controlled the line of scrimmage for Tennessee’s defense last week, and we expect him to be in Deshaun Watson’s face all day this Sunday. The Browns will struggle to run the ball without Quinshon Judkins, and this game will come down to a key turnover or special teams play. Since it’s a game that can go either way, we’re backing the home team here to get their second win. Final Score: Titans 16 – Browns 13 MORE: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 6 Cincinnati Bengals over the Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Bur

Final Score: Titans 16 – Browns 13 MORE: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 6 Cincinnati Bengals over the Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) plays withh a wrapped left half in the third quarter of the NFL Week 5 game between the Miami Dolphins and the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. The Bengals improved to 3-2 on the season with a 31-24 win on the road. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Bengals return from their bye with their receiving corps fully healthy and ready to go, while the Ravens come limping home after a loss in their second straight game without Lamar Jackson to the Browns. The jury is still out on whether or not Baltimore will get their two-time MVP QB back this week, but either way the Bengals are going to come in with all pistons popping. These two teams have played in some exciting shootouts in the past, and if that happens again this Sunday, it should be the Bengals that come out on top. Look for Joe Burrow to connect with both Ja’marr Chase and Tee Higgins early and often, keeping the Bengals far enough ahead to limit Derrick Henry’s damage to their defense. Final Score: Bengals 31 – Ravens 27 Las Vegas Raiders over the Los Angeles Rams Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams (17) makes a catch for a touchdown as Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (22) defends during the second quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Rams are still riding on reputation, as they remain the consensus pick to win this game on the road despite another loss to their record and offense last week, as they dropped a shocker to the Cardinals and lost Devante Adams to a tendon tear. Both types of losses are piling up for the Rams as they now sit at 2-4, and Adams joins Terence Ferguson and Myles Garrett on the IR. The Raiders look for real this season, and they won’t just roll over for Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua. Maxx Crosby will do his best to make this Sunday a long day for the reigning MVP, while Kirk Cousins will do his best to avoid Aaron Donald and get the ball to his playmakers. This could be a signature win for Klint Kubiak and the Raiders as they look to take the next step from a rebuilding franchise to a playoff contender in just a few games. We believe in Kubiak, and we’re going with the home team to pull off the upset. Final Score: Raiders 27 – Rams 24 Philadelphia Eagles over the Dallas Cowboys Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni. Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images. The Monday Night matchup features two NFC East teams that are both absolutely reeling right now. The Eagles have some of an excuse, as injuries, retirements, and trades have weakened their roster, and their offense has struggled to mesh under new OC Sean Mannion. The Cowboys haven’t had as many key injuries, yet they’ve still found ways to lose four of their six games this year. In fact, one of their two wins seems even more like a miracle now, when you think back to how they beat the Ravens a few weeks ago in Rio de Janeiro. The season has been a mess for both teams. The Cowboys are the consensus pick to win this game because the Eagles will now have to rely on Tanner McKee to run their offense for the entire season, as Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the year while he deals with blood clots in his lungs. We think this game will be much closer than most people expect, and we’re giving the Eagles a shot at pulling off the upset in front of their home crowd in this prime-time matchup. The Philly defense is still pretty darn good, and with Saquon Barkley likely to return, the offense might be able to put up points against this leaky Dallas defense. This game feels like a survivor matchup for both teams: the loser drops to 2-5, while the winner moves to 3-4 and likely becomes a low-key favorite to win this division. We’re backing the home team here to pull out a win in what could be an ugly game. item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground: it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. Continue reading...

item.title: Cathinka Tandberg: ‘Spurs fans hate Arsenal. That’s how it is’
item.description: Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry means “It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday. “It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.” Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane admits wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is ‘very stressful’ for family
item.description: Bayern Munich and England striker is odds-on favourite ‘I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to’ Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and constant questions are driving his family to distraction. But the Bayern Munich and England striker accepts the suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show. Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. This time out, he has 10 for Bayern and six for England. He scored from the penalty spot in Wednesday night’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, although his stand-out moment was the inch-perfect through ball that set up Alphonso Davies to make it 1-1. Continue reading...

item.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
item.description: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.” Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sam Dalling
item.content:encoded: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of their aim to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

Arsenal had led through Eberechi Eze, who came on in the 10th minute for the stricken Saka, before Harry Kane took centre stage. item.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Florian Wirtz takes on more responsibility in Liverpool’s attack while Pierre Sage is under pressure at Crystal Palace Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s physicality overpowering Bryan Mbeumo in Manchester United’s area at a corner grabbed him a fifth goal in 10 outings for Leeds: a pretty respectable ratio. “I just tried to cause a ruckus,” said Leeds’ No 9. “I make it difficult for the defender. I read the flight of the ball and was quickest to react. I feel really comfortable [here]. I feel the support from the club and the fans and it is a great feeling stepping on to the pitch, particularly at Elland Road.” Of the contenders to be understudy to Harry Kane as England’s centre-forward, Calvert-Lewin may be the lead act – if he can stay injury-free, which has been a difficulty throughout his career. item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
